entries.name: During
entries.doc:
When in the loop a move happens: [from, to] as shares of the loop (0 to 1). The move's `times` then fit between the
two, and for the rest of the loop the bone waits as the move starts and ends: a sprout or drift at nothing, a sway,
bob or pulse where its `phase` leaves it. `from` may be later than `to`, for a move that runs across the loop's
seam. This is how a scene tells a story: something appears at one moment, waves once at another and is gone.

entries.doc: Every move repeats a whole number of `times` in the loop (or in its `during`), so the scene loops.

props.doc:
Casts shadows, worked out once when the scene is built, so they cost nothing as it plays and flicker with it. Only
the first four lights can, and not one that goes round a circle. Give it to a lamp or fire out in the open: a light
set inside something (a jar, a window, a hollow) to stand for its glow would shade everything outside.

this shades it. A light in a small hollow (a stone lantern's light box) sets it to the hollow's size, or the stone
right round it is taken for part of the lamp and lets the light through.

modules.title: Water in a scene written as data

entries.name: SceneWater
entries.doc:
The water of a scene written as data (`SceneDoc.water`), played as the scene plays: from the time alone.

A scene repeats, and can be shown at any moment of its loop in any order (paused, stepped frame by frame to record
it), so its water can't be stepped along with the clock. Instead one whole loop of it is worked out here, once:
the pond (water.ts, the wave equation on a grid) is run through the loop with every raindrop of the scene's rain
splashing where and when it lands and every body the scene names pushing its own volume aside as its bone carries
it through the surface. It is run through a few loops first, so that the rings still crossing the pond when the
loop starts are the ones the end of the loop leaves, and the last run is kept as heights at `fps` moments a
second. `show` then lays the heights for a time back on the pond and shapes and colors the surface's blobs.

Nothing is drawn or keyed by hand: change the rain, the banks or a fish's path and the rings follow.

ctor.code: new SceneWater(scene: CompiledScene, options?: { fps?: number; warm?: number })

props.doc: The scene's water as it was planned.

props.name: water
props.doc: The pond: its grid, and its heights at the time last shown.

props.name: surface

props.name: loop

methods.name: set
methods.doc: Lays the water as it stands `t` seconds into the loop back on the pond (`water.h`), blended between the two kept moments round it.

methods.name: show
methods.doc:
Makes the surface's blobs ready for the scene at `t` seconds, seen from `eye`: lifted and tilted to the water,
and colored for that eye. `mirror` is a picture of what the water mirrors (`SplatMirror`), `lights` the lamps
whose glints it catches. Hand `surface` to `SplatWorld.reshape` (or `Stage.reshape`) afterward.

signatures.code: show(t: number, eye: ArrayLike<number>, options?: { mirror?: MirrorImage | null; lights?: readonly PointLight[] }): void

entries.name: Shape
entries.doc:
A voxel builder for pixel-art scenes: shapes given as distance functions are
cut into a grid, and every grid cell on a shape's surface becomes one small,
nearly solid blob, a disc lying flat on the surface. Drawn small and snapped to a palette (pixelPass.ts)
a scene of these reads as chunky pixel art with real depth.

Where body.ts scatters flat blobs over a creature's skin and blends them
between bones, this fills a regular grid and hangs each part on one bone, so
parts move rigidly (a lamp turns, a boat bobs) and the grid stays crisp.

Light is baked into the colors: one sun, an ambient floor, and shadows cast
by every part on every other, found by marching from each blob toward the
sun through the scene's shapes in the rest pose. `glow` parts keep their
color and cast no shadow. Three optional touches a pixel artist would paint
(all off unless the light asks): `ramp` turns shade cool and light warm
instead of only darker, `crevice` darkens what is shut in by other surfaces,
and `wear` lightens edges. A part's `grime` collects where it is shut in.

props.name: sdf
props.type: (x: number, y: number, z: number) => number
props.doc: Distance to the surface: negative inside.

props.name: min
props.doc: A box that holds the whole shape.

props.name: max
props.doc: The far corner of a box that holds it.

props.name: pieceAt
props.doc:
For a shape made of many pieces (the bricks of a wall, the posts of a fence, the columns of a basalt
causeway): which piece a surface point belongs to, as a whole number 0 or more, or -1 for what lies between
them (mortar). The `pieces` paint gives every piece a color of its own.

entries.name: VoxelPart
entries.doc: One part of a voxel scene: a shape, its paint and the bone that carries it.

props.name: shape
props.doc: The part's shape, as a distance function.

props.name: color
props.doc: Color (0–1, sRGB) or color at a surface point given its outward normal.

props.name: bone
props.doc: The bone that carries it.

props.name: glow
props.doc: Unlit and casting no shadow: lamps, windows, beams of light.

props.name: opacity
props.doc: How solid its blobs are, 0–1.

props.name: noShadow
props.doc: Casts no shadow on other parts (thin things far from the ground, like birds).

props.name: grime
props.doc: A color (sRGB, 0–1) that gathers in its hollows and creases, as moss or dirt does. Needs the light's `crevice` to find them.

props.name: bare
props.doc: Takes none of the scene's `cover`: water, glass, anything that moves through it or was just made.

props.name: ink
props.doc: Little drawn marks over the surface: see Ink.

props.name: glass
props.doc: Water, ice or glass: see Glass. Needs the spec's `eye`.

props.name: strokes
props.doc:
Dabs that follow the form: 0 leaves each cell a round disc; up to 1 draws it as a stroke along the level line
round the shape, as a painter's brush goes round a pot or a trunk. Seen as blobs it reads as brushwork; in pixel
mode it barely shows.

entries.name: Glass
entries.doc:
A surface you see into and that mirrors what is over it, baked for one place to look from (the spec's `eye`, the
scene's camera): pixel mode cuts anything faint, so instead of being drawn see-through, each cell takes the color
of what lies behind it on the line from the eye (`see`) and of what its mirror line meets (`mirror`, stronger at a
glancing look, as on real water). Seen from far off the scene's own view it is a painting of glass, not glass.

props.name: see
props.doc: How much of what is behind shows through: 0 to 1.

props.name: mirror
props.doc: How much it mirrors, looked at straight on; more at a glancing look. 0 to 1.

props.name: top
props.doc: Only its upturned faces: a pond cut as one slab whose sides are earth.

entries.name: Ink
entries.doc:
Inked detail: the surface is taken in blocks of 4×4 cells (one picture pixel each in pixel mode), and a share of
the blocks (`amount`) each carry one small mark of the kind, picked, turned and flipped at random per block and with
the blocks of each row shifted, so a big wall never shows a repeat. `color` is the ink; left out, a darker step of
the paint under it.

props.name: kind
props.doc: Which marks.

props.name: amount
props.doc: The share of blocks that take a mark, 0–1.

props.name: color
props.doc: The marks' color (sRGB, 0–1); left out, a much darker step of the paint.

entries.name: InkKind
entries.doc: The kinds of mark a part's `ink` can draw on it.

entries.name: INK_MARKS
entries.doc: The marks of each kind, 4×4, top row first. Kinds in UPRIGHT only ever flip side to side: grass grows up, wood grain runs along.

entries.name: inkedAt
entries.doc: Whether the cell at grid (gx, gy, gz) with normal `n` carries ink of this kind: see Ink. `seed` keeps parts apart.

signatures.code: inkedAt(ink: Ink, gx: number, gy: number, gz: number, n: Vec3, seed: number): boolean

entries.name: inkOf
entries.doc: The ink a color takes by default: a darker, slightly richer step of it.

entries.name: Cover
entries.doc:
Something laid over the whole scene once it is cut: `snow` settles on tops that the sky can reach, `moss` creeps
over shut-in and up-turned faces in patches, `dust` lies thin on every upturned face, under cover or not.

props.name: kind
props.doc: What lies on the scene.

props.name: color
props.doc: sRGB, 0–1.

props.name: amount
props.doc: 0–1: how much of the scene it takes, from a dusting to most of what faces up.

entries.name: LooseBlob
entries.doc:
A blob placed as it is, not cut from a shape: soft, faint things in the air such as mist or a beam of light. Kept
under LOOSE_MAX opacity, so pixel mode's map of parts never takes one for a surface.

props.name: center
props.doc: Where it is.

props.name: scale
props.doc: Its radii along x, y and z.

props.name: color
props.doc: Its color (sRGB, 0–1).

props.name: opacity
props.doc: How solid it is, 0–1.

props.name: bone
props.doc: The bone that carries it.

entries.name: Beam
entries.doc:
A beam of light falling through the scene, as from a window or a gap in the leaves: surfaces inside it that face
back up it are lit by its color, on top of the sun, so the beam shows where it lands.

props.name: from
props.doc: Where it starts.

props.name: to
props.doc: Where it lands.

props.name: r
props.doc: Its radius.

props.name: color
props.doc: Its color (sRGB, 0–1).

entries.name: LOOSE_MAX
entries.doc: The most a loose blob may cover: under the engine's PART_CUT, so it never shows in the map of parts.

entries.name: VoxelLight
entries.doc: The light baked into a voxel scene's colors: the sun, the ambient light, cast shadows and the painted touches.

props.name: dir
props.doc: Direction toward the sun.

props.name: ambient
props.doc: Light that reaches everywhere, 0–1.

props.name: shadow
props.doc: How dark a cast shadow is: 0 leaves no shadow, 1 leaves only the ambient light.

props.name: ramp
props.doc: How far shade turns its hue toward cool violet and full sun toward warm yellow, as a painter's ramp does: 0 only darkens.

props.name: crevice
props.doc: How much surfaces shut in by others (corners, cracks, the foot of a wall) darken: 0 to 1.

props.name: wear
props.doc: How much sharp outer edges lighten, as worn stone and wood do: 0 to 1.

props.name: bounce
props.doc: How much color surfaces throw onto what faces them, as a red wall warms the floor beside it: 0 to 1.

props.name: steps
props.doc:
Painted in steps: once a blob's light is worked out, its color is moved onto one color of `palette` (sRGB, 0–1), a
step of its own paint's ramp (the palette colors that paint passes through from deep shade to full sun), so shade
falls in flat bands a pixel pass has nothing left to guess at. `mottle` (0–1, `MOTTLE` when left out) nudges small
patches a little lighter or darker first, so a band's edge is ragged as a brush leaves it, not ruled. Parts that
`glow` keep their color.

entries.name: STEP_L
entries.doc: How much a difference in lightness counts beside one in hue when a blob picks its step (`stepper`): under 1, so hue is kept first.

entries.name: MOTTLE
entries.doc: How ragged the edge between two steps is, where a scene doesn't say (`VoxelLight.steps`).

entries.name: HUE_KEEP
entries.doc:
How far round the hue circle (degrees, in OKLab) a palette color may sit from a paint's own and still be a step of its
ramp (`stepper`), where both have color enough to have a hue (`HUE_FROM`). A red that has no darker red in the palette
stays its own darkest red in shade rather than turning brown or orange, as a hand-made ramp would.

entries.name: HUE_FROM
entries.doc: The chroma (OKLab) under which a color counts as a gray for `HUE_KEEP`: a gray is a step of any paint's ramp.

entries.name: GRAY_TURN
entries.doc:
How far round the hue circle (degrees) a near-gray palette color may sit from the way a gray paint's light tints it
(cool in shade, warm in sun) or from the paint's own faint hue, and still be a step of its ramp (`stepper`). White
sails in shade took the sky's palest blue, which read as holes through to the sky.

entries.name: ESCAPE
entries.doc: How many times closer a palette color off a paint's ramp must be before a blob takes it (`stepper`): only light of another color carries a blob that far.

entries.name: VoxelSpec
entries.doc: A voxel scene for `buildVoxels`: its bones, its parts and the grid's cell size.

props.name: bones
props.doc: The scene's bones.

props.name: parts
props.doc: The parts, all cut into one shared grid.

props.name: spacing
props.doc: Grid cell size in world units: one blob per surface cell.

props.name: light
props.doc: The baked light; what is left out comes from `DEFAULT_LIGHT`.

props.name: blocks
props.doc: Skip blocks of cells far from a surface: much quicker for big smooth shapes, sound only for honest distance functions (sculpt.ts).

props.name: trueShell
props.doc:
Keep the outermost layer one cell thick in true distance, not in the shape's own units. A shape pushed in and
out (`displace`) can have a distance that changes faster than one unit per unit; read raw, its layer comes out
thinner than a cell and leaves holes you see the far side through. Creatures (sculpt.ts) turn this on.

props.name: keepBuried
props.doc: How deep (world units) a cell may sit inside a neighbor on its bone and still be made: a skirt that keeps a joint closed as parts move.

props.name: disc
props.doc:
A disc's radius (its blob's scale across the surface) as a share of `spacing`. The default leaves the grid
crisp for pixel mode, which cuts alpha; drawn smooth, discs that small let about a tenth of what lies behind
show between them, so a creature seen as blobs wants them wider.

props.name: loose
props.doc: Blobs placed as they are, after the cut ones: see LooseBlob.

props.name: beams
props.doc: Beams of light that fall through the scene.

props.name: cover
props.doc: Snow, moss or dust over every part that isn't `bare` or `glow`: see Cover.

props.name: focus
props.doc:
Where the eye goes: within `r` of `at` the grid is as fine as `spacing`; further out it is twice as coarse, with
discs twice the size, so the subject keeps its detail and the rest is painted broadly in a quarter of the blobs. Only parts at least
eight cells across every way go coarse: a thinner one could miss every coarse cell.

props.name: eye
props.doc: Where `glass` parts are looked at from: the scene's camera.

props.name: sky
props.doc: The sky a `glass` part mirrors where its mirror line meets nothing: [overhead, at the horizon]. Dark when left out.

props.name: lamps
props.doc:
Lamps whose shadows are baked, in the order of the live lights they stand for (at most four; a gap is a light
that casts none): for each blob, how much of lamp k it can see goes in byte k of `seen`, and the engine's live
light pass scales that light by it, so a lamp's shadows flicker with it and cost nothing a frame.

entries.name: Lamp
entries.doc: A light that stays put, whose shadows `buildVoxels` works out once for each blob.

props.name: at
props.doc: Where it is.

props.name: reach
props.doc: How far its light reaches: blobs further off are not looked at (their byte stays full).

props.name: clear
props.doc:
How far short of it the look toward it stops, so its own housing doesn't shade everything: `LAMP_CLEAR` where
left out. Blobs nearer than this are always lit. Set it to the room round a lamp that sits in a small hollow,
or the hollow's own walls and roof let its light through.

entries.name: MAX_LAMPS
entries.doc: How many lamps' shadows a blob carries, one byte each.

entries.name: LIT_MAX
entries.doc:
The brightest the baked sun makes a surface, as a share of its color. Only
`glow` parts are built brighter, so pixel mode can tell a lamp from a white
wall in the sun (GLOW_FROM in splat-core/pixel.ts sits just over it). Live
lights add on top: a surface under a strong one does pass the line and glow.

entries.name: PAINTED
entries.doc: The painted touches pixel scenes use unless they say otherwise: hue-turning shade, dark crevices, worn edges.
entries.type: { ramp: number; crevice: number; wear: number }

entries.name: DEFAULT_LIGHT
entries.doc: The light a voxel scene gets where it sets none of its own.

entries.name: sphere
entries.doc: A ball of radius `r` about `c`.

entries.name: ellipsoid
entries.doc: An ellipsoid with radii along x, y and z (the distance is approximate, exact on the surface).

entries.name: box
entries.doc: A box with half sizes `h`, its edges rounded by `round`.

signatures.code: box(c: Vec3, h: Vec3, round?: number): Shape

entries.name: cone
entries.doc: A rounded cone from a (radius ra) to b (radius rb); equal radii make a capsule.

signatures.code: cone(a: Vec3, b: Vec3, ra: number, rb?: number): Shape

entries.name: cylinder
entries.doc: A upright cylinder with flat ends, from y0 to y1; `r1` tapers it.

signatures.code: cylinder(c: [x: number, z: number], y0: number, y1: number, r0: number, r1?: number): Shape

entries.name: torus
entries.doc: A ring lying flat (about the y axis): `R` to the middle of the tube, `r` the tube's radius.

signatures.code: torus(c: Vec3, R: number, r: number): Shape

entries.name: roof
entries.doc: A roof: a ridge along x at `top`, sloping down to `y0` at `hz` either side.

signatures.code: roof(c: [x: number, z: number], y0: number, top: number, hx: number, hz: number): Shape

entries.name: union
entries.doc: Several shapes as one: a point inside any of them is inside.

entries.name: tighten
entries.doc:
A shape whose distance can overstate by up to 1/k − 1 of itself (a ragged edge, an overhang the side distance
doesn't see) made honest for the sun march: exact within `near` of the surface, where cells are placed, and
scaled by k beyond it, so a step never passes through.

signatures.code: tighten(s: Shape, k: number, near?: number): Shape

entries.name: many
entries.doc:
A union of many scattered shapes, sorted into buckets so a point asks only the shapes near it: quick for fences,
fallen bricks and twigs.

entries.name: orientedBox
entries.doc:
A box turned any way: `axes` are its three edge directions (unit length, square to each other) and `half` its half
size along each. Fallen bricks, leaning posts, rails between them.

signatures.code: orientedBox(c: Vec3, axes: [Vec3, Vec3, Vec3], h: Vec3, round?: number): Shape

entries.name: BlendKind
entries.doc: How a `blend` meets where its shapes touch: a rounded fillet, a flat bevel, or a run of little steps.

entries.name: blend
entries.doc: Shapes joined so the seam between them is filled in: `r` is how far the fillet, bevel or stairs reach.

signatures.code: blend(kind: BlendKind, r: number, shapes: Shape[], steps?: number): Shape

entries.name: lathe
entries.doc:
A turned shape, as from a lathe: `profile` is [radius, height] pairs from the bottom up, standing on `c`, and the
outline is spun about the upright axis through it. Vases, bells, bottles, chess pieces, lamp posts.

entries.name: sweep
entries.doc: A tube along a path of points, `r0` thick at the start and `r1` at the end: vines, pipes, rails, a dragon's tail.

signatures.code: sweep(path: Vec3[], r0: number, r1?: number): Shape

entries.name: LETTERS
entries.doc: The 3×5 letters `pixelText` knows, top row first.

entries.name: pixelText
entries.doc:
Words in blocky 3×5 letters (`LETTERS`; lower case is read as upper), `size` tall and `depth` thick, centered on
`at` and reading along +x, or along -z when `facing` is 'x'. A letter needs about five grid cells of height to read.

signatures.code: pixelText(at: Vec3, text: string, size: number, depth: number, facing?: "z" | "x"): Shape

entries.name: letterGrid
entries.doc:
A model drawn as letters: `layers` from the bottom up, each a list of rows from the back (-z) to the front, each
row a string read along +x; any character but '.' or a space fills a cube `size` across. Standing on `at`, centered
on it across. `letterAt` says which letter a point is in, so a paint can color the model by letter.

signatures.code: letterGrid(at: Vec3, size: number, layers: string[][]): Shape & { letterAt: (p: Vec3, n: Vec3) => string | undefined }

entries.name: cut
entries.doc: `a` with `b` cut out of it.

entries.name: displace
entries.doc: A shape pushed in or out by `f(x, y, z)` world units: ripples, rough rock. `reach` is the most it moves.

signatures.code: displace(s: Shape, f: (x: number, y: number, z: number) => number, reach: number): Shape

entries.name: coverAt
entries.doc:
How much of a cover lies on a surface point, 0–1. `open` is its openness (moss wants it low) and `sky` how much
of the sky straight up it sees (snow wants it high); each is only asked for when the kind needs it.

signatures.code: coverAt(cover: Cover, p: Vec3, n: Vec3, spacing: number, open: () => number, sky: () => number): number

entries.name: bakedColor
entries.doc:
A surface color under the baked light. `shade` is how bright (0 to LIT_MAX), `lit` how much straight sun it takes
(0–1). With `ramp` the color doesn't only darken: shade turns its hue toward violet and gains a little chroma in the
middle tones, full sun leans warm, and even a gray goes cool in shadow, so a palette's cool darks get picked over its
browns. `lift` lightens it (a worn edge). Never brighter than LIT_MAX, which keeps it under pixel mode's glow line.

signatures.code: bakedColor(base: Vec3, shade: number, lit: number, ramp: number, lift?: number): Vec3

entries.name: stepper
entries.doc:
Painting in steps (`VoxelLight.steps`): gives the function that moves a blob's finished color onto its paint's ramp.
A paint's ramp is the palette colors it passes through as its light goes from a deep corner to full sun (found once
per paint, to 1/64 a channel); a finished color takes the nearest of them, after `mottle` has pushed its lightness up
or down by patch. Light of another color (a beam, a bounce, a mirror) can carry a blob well off its ramp: when a
palette color outside it is `ESCAPE` times as close or more, that one is taken. A ramp keeps to its paint's own hue (`HUE_KEEP`). Palette colors over `LIT_MAX` are held at
it, as every lit color is, so nothing painted starts to glow.

signatures.code: stepper(steps: { palette: Vec3[]; mottle?: number }, light: VoxelLight): (base: Vec3, color: Vec3, i: number, j: number, k: number) => Vec3

entries.name: unlit
entries.doc:
Runs `make` with every `buildVoxels` inside it leaving the light out: each blob keeps its paint (with its ink, cover
and grime, which are paint), and no sun, shade, cast shadow, ramp, crevice, wear, bounce or beam is baked into it.
For a look that lights the blobs itself, such as cel shading (`Stage.setCel`), which would otherwise shade a shadow
twice. It reaches builders that take no light of their own to set, such as a creature's `make`.

entries.name: banded
entries.doc:
Runs `make` with every `buildVoxels` inside it lighting each blob as one texel in `n` flat bands: the sun's share that
reaches a blob (its facing times its cast shadow) is moved onto the nearest of `n` steps from none to full before its
color is worked out, so light and shade fall in whole blobs, crisp along the surface, while each blob keeps its own
paint (bricks, planks, ripples). The ambient share is left as it is. 0 or 1 leaves the light smooth.

entries.name: hugged
entries.doc:
Runs `make` with every `buildVoxels` inside it fitting the discs along a shape's outer edges to the edge: a disc whose
surface ends within its reach (the shape falls away from the disc's own plane, as past the top of a fence rail or the
rim of a pond) is moved in and squeezed across the edge, long along it, so the row of discs ends in a straight line
where the shape does instead of a row of round bumps standing past it. Inner corners are left alone: what meets them
covers them. See `edgeFit`.

entries.name: edgeFit
entries.doc:
Where the surface of a shape ends within a disc's reach, in the disc's own plane: the way out to the nearest outer edge
(a unit vector in the plane) and how far from the disc's middle the edge lies, or undefined when the surface carries on
all round. `past(q)` is how far the shape lies off the disc's plane at `q`, counted as off past `least`; it is asked at
three distances along `EDGE_WAYS` ways, the nearer ones only where the farthest finds an edge.

signatures.code: edgeFit(p: Vec3, n: Vec3, reach: number, past: (q: Vec3) => number, least: number): { out: Vec3; at: number } | undefined

entries.name: bandOf
entries.doc: Moves a sun share (0 to 1) onto the nearest of `n` steps (`banded`).

entries.name: buildVoxels
entries.doc:
Builds the scene's blobs, skin and skeleton. Cells sit on one grid shared by
every part (multiples of `spacing` from the origin), so parts line up, and
the same spec always gives the same blobs.

modules.title: Built things: walls, steps, fences, arcades
modules.doc:
Built things: walls of real bricks, flights of worn steps, fences along a path and arcades cut into
equal bays, each one shape however many pieces it has. Pure numbers and distance functions, so the scene builder
cuts them like any other shape, and each shape's `pieceAt` says which brick, block, post or stone a point is on,
for the `pieces` paint.

Every piece is placed by a rule from the shape's own sizes and a seed (the same seed, the same ruin), and sizes are
fitted so the pieces come out whole: a wall's length is a whole number of bricks (half bricks at the ends of every
other course), a span a whole number of bays, so pillars and posts land exactly at its ends.

The idea comes from Silicon Jungle's Ink Studio built-things kit; this is our own code.

signatures.code: hash(seed: number, a: number, b?: number, c?: number): number

entries.name: noise1

signatures.code: noise1(seed: number, u: number, size: number): number

modules.title: Formations: crystals, columns, drips
modules.doc:
Formations: shapes that come from a rule rather than placing each one by hand. A faceted crystal and
clusters of them from one root, a geode broken open, basalt columns on a hex grid, stalactites and stalagmites that
join into columns, flowstone down a wall, and icicles under every downward edge of another shape. Pure distance
functions, each with a `pieceAt` for the `pieces` paint.

The idea comes from Silicon Jungle's Ink Studio formations kit; this is our own code.

modules.title: Living forms: trees, cacti, shells
modules.doc:
Living forms: trees grown by space colonization, ribbed cacti, succulent rosettes, bracket fungi,
brain coral, shells wound on a log spiral, horns that curl, antlers with tines and a spine of ribs. Pure numbers and
distance functions: each lights, shadows, grows (on a bone with a `sprout` move) and rigs like any other part.

The idea comes from Silicon Jungle's Ink Studio living-forms kit; this is our own code.

entries.doc: A tree for `tree`, grown by space colonization.

props.name: height
props.doc: How high the trunk rises before the crown.

props.name: crown

props.name: r

props.name: r

entries.name: colonize
entries.doc:
Grows a tree by space colonization: points are scattered through the crown, and every point pulls the nearest
branch tip toward it until a branch reaches it. Then each limb is made as thick as what it carries (the pipe rule:
a limb's radius to the 2.5 is the sum of its children's), scaled so the trunk's foot is `r`.

signatures.code: colonize(s: TreeSpec): { nodes: TreeNode[]; ends: number[] }

modules.title: Worn land
modules.doc:
Worn land and layered rock: a height field worn by water and slumping (droplets carve gullies and drop
what they carry in fans; slopes too steep for their rock slide to scree), rock laid down in beds where soft beds wear
back further than hard ones, so ledges, benches and overhangs come by themselves, with hoodoos and natural arches as
presets; cracked mud whose plates curl at their edges; and pebbles along a stream bed, bigger where it runs fastest.

Everything runs once, when the scene is built, from its numbers and a seed: the same seed, the same land. Erosion
has a budget (`MAX_DROPS`, a grid of at most `MAX_GRID` cells a side) so a build stays within a second or so.

The idea comes from Silicon Jungle's Ink Studio erosion kit; this is our own code.

Growers: a tree, a coral or a cluster of crystals grown by a branching rule from a seed, so the same
seed always gives the same plant. Pure numbers: `grow` gives the twigs (round-ended sticks, thick to thin) and the
tips, which the scene builder turns into shapes. Each style is a rule: how many branches split from each end, how
far they lean out, how much shorter and thinner each step is, and how hard they pull back toward the sky.

modules.title: Weather that lands
modules.doc:
Weather that lands: what falls finds the ground actually under it, snow lies in drifts shaped by the
wind and what stands in its way, and frost grows across a pane a branch at a time. Pure and tested.

The idea comes from Silicon Jungle's Ink Studio weather kit; this is our own code.

entries.doc:
The height of the first surface met going straight down from `top` at (x, z), or `bottom` if nothing is met. The
shapes' distances are lower bounds, so each step down is as long as the distance says and never steps through.

modules.title: The sky through a day
modules.doc:
The sky over a scene through a day: where the sun and the moon stand for a time, a latitude and a day of the year,
and the light that follows from it, ready for `setLights`. The sun's path is the real one (declination by the day,
hour angle by the clock); its color comes from how much air its light crosses (red and dim at the horizon, white
overhead); the sky's own light, the sky's colors and the stars follow the sun's height. The moon is kept simple: it
trails the sun by its age, a full one rides high in winter and low in summer, and it gives light by how much of it
is lit. Pure numbers, so a page, a test and a recording get the same sky.

Directions are in the scene's frame: +x east, +y up, +z south. Strengths are set for a picture, not for a light
meter: real moonlight is a millionth of sunlight, and an eye (or a camera) opens up at night, so here the night is
dim, not black.

entries.doc: Where and when the sky is: what `daylight` needs besides the hour.

entries.name: Daylight
entries.doc: The sky at one moment, from `daylight`. Colors are linear RGB; a light's color already holds its strength.

props.name: sun

props.name: sunHeight
props.doc: The sun's height over the horizon, in degrees (negative when it is down).

props.name: sunColor
props.doc: The sun's light: white overhead, redder and weaker toward the horizon, nothing once it is down.

props.doc: The way toward the moon (a unit vector).

props.name: moonHeight
props.doc: The moon's height over the horizon, in degrees.

props.name: moonLit
props.doc: How much of the moon's face is lit, 0 (new) to 1 (full).

props.name: ambient
props.doc: Light from the whole sky, which reaches into shade: blue by day, warm at dusk, dim and blue at night.

props.name: zenith
props.doc: The sky's color straight up.

props.name: horizon
props.doc: The sky's color at the horizon, away from the sun.

props.name: sunGlow
props.doc: The warm glow low in the sky round the sun as it rises and sets: nothing while it is high or well down.

props.name: stars
props.doc: How clearly the stars show, 0 by day to 1 in full night (less under a bright moon).

props.name: dark
props.doc: How dark it has grown, 0 in daylight to 1 once the sun is well down: when lamps come on.

entries.name: skyWay
entries.doc:
The way toward a point of the sky (a unit vector: +x east, +y up, +z south) from its hour angle (degrees west of
due south, 15 an hour), its declination (degrees north of the sky's equator) and the latitude it is seen from.

signatures.code: skyWay(hourAngle: number, declination: number, latitude: number): Vec3

entries.name: sunDeclination
entries.doc: How far north of the sky's equator the sun is on a day of the year, in degrees: 23.44 at the June solstice.

entries.name: sunWay
entries.doc: The way toward the sun at an hour of the day (0 to 24 by the sun: 12 is when it is highest).

entries.name: moonWay
entries.doc:
The way toward the moon at an hour of the day. It trails the sun across the sky by its age (a full moon is opposite
the sun, so it rises as the sun sets), and its declination is the sun's turned by its age, so a full moon is high in
winter and low in summer.

entries.name: moonLit
entries.doc: How much of the moon's face is lit at an age: 0 new, 1 full.

entries.name: sunTimes
entries.doc:
When the sun rises and sets, in hours by the sun, from where its center crosses the horizon. Where it never sets
(a polar summer) `rise` is 0 and `set` 24; where it never rises, both are 12.

signatures.code: sunTimes(place?: SkyPlace): { rise: number; set: number }

entries.name: airMass
entries.doc:
How much air light crosses on its way down from a height over the horizon (degrees), as a multiple of the air
straight overhead: 1 at the zenith, about 38 at the horizon (Kasten and Young's fit).

entries.name: daylight
entries.doc:
The sky and its light at an hour of the day (0 to 24 by the sun; any number wraps) at a place: where the sun and
moon stand, their light, the sky's own light and colors, how clearly stars show and how dark it has grown. Every
value changes smoothly through the day, so an hour hand dragged across it never jumps.

entries.name: skyLights
entries.doc:
The lights a sky gives a scene, for `setLights`: the sun and the moon as lights from a direction (each only while
it gives light, so a march for shadows is never spent on a light that is down), casting shadows if asked, and the
sky's own light as the ambient color.

signatures.code: skyLights(sky: Daylight, shadows?: boolean): { lights: { direction: Vec3; color: Vec3; shadow: boolean }[]; ambient: Vec3 }

entries.name: PixelPass
entries.doc:
Pixel mode: the scene is drawn small into a target, and one full-screen pass
turns it into pixel art and scales it up in whole pixels, with no smoothing.

The pass is the GPU twin of `pixelArt` in splat-core/pixel.ts (change one,
change both): alpha cut, glow from bright pixels, nearest palette color in
OKLab with a Bayer dither, edge lines inside the scene, an outline on the
empty pixels that touch it, and a sky behind. It runs once per art pixel,
into `art`, which keeps display (sRGB) color so a palette color is stored
exactly; the screen then gets a plain copy, scaled up. The art of the frame
before is kept too: a look with `steady` reads it so a pixel between two
palette colors does not flip from frame to frame.

A look with `fine` draws the scene and its map of parts at twice the art's
size first, and a step before the pass settles each art pixel from its four
samples into `small` and `ids` (`resolveFine` in pixel.ts is its twin), so
everything after it is the same either way.

props.name: small
props.doc: The scene, drawn small. Linear and premultiplied, as any render target.

props.name: ids
props.doc: The scene's parts, drawn small (`SplatWorld.parts`): where the color changes, one part ends and another begins. Only drawn for a look with `parts`.

props.name: ranks
props.doc: Each art pixel's step of the dither pattern, from the blob there (red, a byte), for a look with `surface`.

props.name: fineSmall
props.doc: The scene and its map of parts at twice the art's size, for a look with `fine`: what `small` and `ids` are settled from.

props.name: fineIds
props.doc:
The map of parts at twice the art's size, which four samples a pixel settles from (its first texture), and in the
same draw the picture with every blob a hard disc in its own color, as the map cuts it (its second, read with
`PixelLook.solid`): one draw of every blob for both, which on a phone is most of what either costs.

props.name: art
props.doc: The finished art at its own size, in display color, for reading back (tests, saving) and for the screen.

props.name: before
props.doc: The art of the frame before, when this frame was drawn against it (a look with `steady`): what `pixelArt` needs to give the same answer.

props.name: look
props.doc: The look in use.

props.name: drawnAt
props.doc: The time the last frame was drawn for (`setTime`): what `pixelArt` needs as its `time`.

props.name: width
props.doc: The art's width, in art pixels.

props.name: height
props.doc: The art's height, in art pixels.

methods.name: reset
methods.doc: Forgets the frame before: for when what is being drawn is swapped for something else.

methods.name: setLook
methods.doc: Changes the look: palette, dither, glow, lines.

methods.name: setTime
methods.doc: The scene's time for this frame: what heat haze's waves and color cycling step by (`pixelArt`'s `time`).

methods.name: setGlitch
methods.doc:
This frame's glitch, laid on as the art goes to the screen (the art itself, `art`, stays clean: `glitchArt` lays
the same on a frame read back). Left out, none.

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: The art's size in pixels.

methods.name: render
methods.doc:
Draws `scene` as pixel art. With `screen` (the output's size in device
pixels and how many of them make one art pixel) it goes to the renderer's
current output; without, into `art` at one to one.

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera, screen?: { width: number; height: number; scale: number }): void

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees its render targets.

modules.title: Pixel art
modules.doc:
The 2D half of Splat to Sprite: everything that happens after the splat has
been rendered. Pure functions on RGBA byte arrays so they can be unit tested
without a GPU.

Pipeline per frame:
  supersampled render → box downsample → alpha cut → palette (+dither) →
  stray-pixel cleanup → outline

entries.name: Rgb
entries.doc: A color as three numbers: red, green and blue, 0 to 255 in a palette.

entries.name: Frame
entries.doc: A picture as RGBA bytes.

props.name: width
props.doc: Pixels across.

props.name: height
props.doc: Pixels down.

props.name: data
props.doc: RGBA, row 0 at the top, straight (not premultiplied) alpha.

entries.name: PixelLook
entries.doc: How a scene is turned into pixel art, live (splat-engine/pixelPass.ts) or here on the CPU.

props.name: palette
props.doc: The colors every pixel snaps to; empty keeps the scene's own colors.

props.name: dither
props.doc: 0..1, as for `quantize`.

props.name: outline
props.doc: A 1-pixel line round the scene's silhouette, or none.

props.name: own
props.doc:
The outline in a darker tone of whatever it goes round, not one color for the whole scene: each outline pixel takes
the palette color nearest a darker step of the scene pixel beside it (`outline`'s own color where the palette has
nothing darker). Needs `outline`.

props.name: fine
props.doc:
Four samples a pixel: the scene is drawn at twice the art's size and each art pixel is settled from its 2×2 samples
(`resolveFine`) before anything else happens, so a pixel on the edge of a thing shows one thing or the other, never
a mix. The live pass does it itself; `pixelArt` is given the settled frame.

props.name: glow
props.doc: How far bright pixels spill light onto their neighbors: 0 is none.

props.name: edges
props.doc: Lines inside the scene, where one color meets a much lighter one: 0 (or left out) is none, 1 the darkest line.

props.name: parts
props.doc:
A line where one part of the scene meets another whose color is too close for `edges` to draw one (two things of one color, one in front of the other), at `edges`' strength or full strength without it.
Needs a map of the parts drawn beside the scene (`pixelArt`'s `parts`; the live pass draws its own).

props.name: across
props.doc:
Lines inside the scene only where one thing meets another: with a map of parts (`parts`, or `fine`, which draws one),
a jump in color within one part is its paint (grass, stonework) and takes no line, as a pixel artist outlines things
and not their texture. Without a map it does nothing.

props.name: solid
props.doc:
The scene's picture drawn with every blob a hard disc in its own color, cut where the map of parts cuts it, so a
thing's edge never shows a little of what is behind it (the stage draws it; the picture handed in is already so).

props.name: sky
props.doc:
A backdrop behind the scene: its color at the top and at the bottom of the picture, blended between and dithered into the palette.
`reach` is how far down the picture the blend runs before it is all the bottom color (above 0, up to 1; the whole way when left out or not a sound number: `skyReach`).
Left out, empty pixels stay clear.

props.name: steady
props.doc:
Steady pixels: a pixel keeps the palette color it had in the frame before unless another is closer by more than this (an OKLab distance; 0 or left out is off).
Without it, a pixel that sits between two colors flips back and forth as lights flicker and the view turns.

props.name: tidy
props.doc:
Lone-pixel cleanup, as a pixel artist does it: a scene pixel whose color none of its eight neighbors shares, while
six or more of them share one other color, takes that color. With a map of parts, only a pixel inside its own
part (four or more neighbors of its part) is touched, so a speck, an eye or a firefly in front of something stays.
A checkerboard dither keeps its pixels: each has its own color on the diagonals.

props.name: calm
props.doc:
Calmer pixels, in place of `tidy` (an idea from Silicon Jungle's Ink Studio, whose cleanup pass this follows in
part): a pixel art piece is flat patches of color with dither only where one gives way to the next, while a scene
of small blobs comes out speckled. So, reading only the art as drawn: a scene pixel takes the color `CALM_MOST` or
more of its eight neighbors share when fewer share its own (with a map of parts, only neighbors of its own part
count, so one thing never bleeds into another); a scene pixel with the empty backdrop on three or four sides (a
one-pixel bump on a silhouette) takes the backdrop's color beside it, and an empty pixel with the scene on three or
four sides (a notch) takes the scene's, so an outline runs clean; and lines are cleaned (`lineFix`: one-pixel kinks off
straight edges, doubled pixels off the corners of dark lines); and a patch of one or two pixels joins its
neighbors' color unless it is a highlight or a detail (`SPECK_MOST`, `SPECK_KEEP`). `calmArt` is the CPU twin of the pass.

props.name: flat
props.doc:
Dither only where a pixel artist puts it: the sky's blend and the light a glow spills onto the scene keep `dither`,
while the scene's own surfaces are drawn flat, each pixel its nearest palette color, so shade falls in bands. A
pixel a glow lights snaps only to a color of its own hue, the light's, or a gray (`keptNearest`).

props.name: rim
shine
props.doc: A highlight on the peak of each smooth lit form (`peakAt`): that pixel one step lighter in its own hue.

props.name: surface
props.doc:
Dither that stays on the things it falls on: each blob takes one step of the Bayer pattern from where it sits in
its own rest pose (`ditherRank`), not from the pixel it lands on, so the pattern rides with a turning view or a
moving creature instead of standing still on the screen while they slide under it. Needs a map of each pixel's
step drawn beside the scene (`pixelArt`'s `ranks`; the live pass draws its own). The sky keeps the screen's pattern.
Left out with `flat`: there only a glow's spill is dithered, and the map cost a whole extra draw of every blob.
After Silicon Jungle's Ink Studio (object-space dither, MIT), with their agreement.

props.name: snap
props.doc:
Holds the picture on the art's grid: the world's origin always lands on a whole art pixel, so when the view slides
(a pan, a zoom, a camera that follows) the scene moves by whole pixels instead of smearing across them. The live
pass only (`snapShift`). After Ink Studio's camera snap, which does it for a flat view; here it holds for a
perspective view at the origin's depth.

props.name: bands
props.doc:
Glow in bands (1 or 2): in place of the soft spill round bright pixels, each pixel within `HALO_R` art pixels of a
glowing one takes a flat share of its light by how far it is, in rings, as hand-drawn pixel art lights a lamp.
After Ink Studio's banded glow (MIT), with their agreement.

props.name: heat
props.doc:
Heat haze: pixels above anything glowing (within `HEAT_R` across and up to `HEAT_UP` more above) are drawn from a
pixel or so to one side, the shift running in waves that change `pace` times a second (a whole number a loop, so a
recording joins). `pixels` is the most a pixel moves, 1 to 3. After Ink Studio's heat effect (MIT).

props.name: cycle
props.doc:
Color cycling: scene pixels whose palette color is one of `colors` step along the list `pace` times a second, as
old games ran water and fire. Each color is taken to its nearest in the palette, so a visitor's own palette still
cycles. Steady pixels leave these colors alone. After Ink Studio's palette cycles (MIT).

props.name: selout
props.doc:
Lighter outlines on lit sides ("selout"): an outline beside a scene pixel lighter than `SELOUT_FROM` takes a shade
just under that pixel's own color instead of the outline, so the line shows only where the thing is in shade. Needs
`outline`. After Ink Studio's lit and shadow line colors (MIT).

entries.name: pixelArt
entries.doc:
One frame of a scene to pixel art, the CPU twin of the live pixel pass
(change one, change both). `f` is the scene drawn small: straight sRGB.

  alpha cut → glow (bright pixels light their neighbors, and empty pixels
  beside them) → edge lines (the darker side of a jump in color) →
  palette + dither → outline on the empty pixels that touch the scene →
  sky on the rest, if the look has one

`before` is the art of the frame before, for a look with `steady`: where it
holds a palette color that is nearly as close as the best one, that pixel
keeps it. `parts` is the scene's map of parts for a look with `parts`: the
same view with every part in its own flat color (alpha 0 where there is none).

signatures.code: pixelArt(f: Frame, look: PixelLook, before?: Frame, parts?: Frame, ranks?: Frame, time?: number): Frame

modules.title: Brush and ink marks
modules.doc:
Marks: every blob drawn as a brush mark or an ink stroke in place of a soft dot, so a scene reads as a painting or
a drawing from any side. A mark is a function of where a pixel is on its own blob (along the blob's long and short
axes on screen, in standard deviations) and of the blob's seed, and of nothing on the screen: marks belong to their
blobs, so they stay put as the view moves, where a filter laid over the finished picture slides across it.

This file is the CPU twin of the engine's draw (`markOf` in splat-engine/engine.ts): change one, change both.

entries.name: MarkKind
entries.doc:
The kinds of mark: flat opaque dabs with bristle streaks, thicker dabs with ridges that catch light, a wash with a
pen stroke along each blob, hatching that is denser where it is darker, or a whole disc of the blob's own color with
no brushwork at all (`flat`: the fill under cel shading, where the discs of one surface close up into one color),
or stippling: pen dots on bare paper, more of them and bigger where it is darker.

entries.name: MARK_KINDS
entries.doc: The kinds, in the order the GPU numbers them (from 1; 0 is no marks).

entries.name: MarkLook
entries.doc: How the blobs are drawn as marks.

props.name: kind
props.doc: Which mark.

props.name: size
props.doc: How big a mark is beside its blob: 1 reaches 1.5 standard deviations along the blob (default 1).

props.name: ink
props.doc: Ink, hatch and stipple: the pen's color, sRGB 0–1 (default a blue-black).

props.name: paper
props.doc: Ink, hatch and stipple: the paper's color, sRGB 0–1 (default a warm white). Set the page behind the view to it too.

props.name: soft
props.doc:
Lay the marks one over another from far to near, with soft edges, as soft blobs are drawn. Without it (the
default) each pixel shows the mark nearest to it, so the marks on a thing keep their places as it turns: right
for anything cut as discs on a surface. A scan's blobs overlap far more and build a surface between them, and
look better laid softly.

entries.name: lineWeight
entries.doc:
How strong a drawn outline is, 0–1: heavier round dark things than light ones, swelling and thinning along its
length (`swell`, 0–1, smooth noise), and broken off here and there round the lightest. `dark` is 1 less the root of
the thing's luminance.

entries.name: OutlinePen
entries.doc: A pen for drawn outlines (`Stage.setOutline`).

props.name: width
props.doc: The line's width in CSS pixels (default 1.5).

props.name: ink
props.doc: Its color, sRGB 0–1 (default the same blue-black as `MarkLook.ink`).

entries.name: MarkSample
entries.doc: What a mark is at one pixel.

props.name: cover
props.doc: How much of the pixel the mark covers, 0–1. Marks are paint: its alpha is this times the blob's opacity times `MARK_SOLID`, at most 1.

props.name: color
props.doc: The mark's color there, linear RGB.

entries.name: markAt
entries.doc:
A mark at (u, v): u along the blob's long axis on screen and v across it, in standard deviations. `rgb` is the
blob's color (linear) and `seed` its own number, 0–1. `ink` and `paper` are linear too.

signatures.code: markAt(kind: MarkKind, u: number, v: number, seed: number, rgb: ArrayLike<number>, size?: number, ink?: ArrayLike<number>, paper?: ArrayLike<number>): MarkSample

entries.name: InkLines
entries.doc:
Drawn outlines, as a pen would put them down: round the subject, where one thing passes in front of another, and
between its parts. Marks (`setMarks`) lay each blob down as a stroke, which shades a picture but never draws its
edges; a pen and wash drawing is the other way round, contours first.

The frame is drawn three times with the same moved and sorted blobs: the picture, a map of depth (`SplatDepth`) and
a map of parts (`SplatWorld.parts`). One pass then inks a pixel when, a line's width away, the picture ends, or
something is clearly nearer, or another part begins. The line is not even: its weight swells and thins along its
length and is heavier against dark things than light ones, where it may break off (`lineWeight` in marks.ts, the
CPU twin of the weight); and it wobbles a little, as a hand does.

props.name: picture
props.doc: The picture, as the stage draws it without lines.

props.name: ids
props.doc: The map of parts the lines between parts come from.

methods.name: setPen
methods.doc: The pen: its color (linear RGB) and how wide its line is, in device pixels.

signatures.code: setPen(ink: readonly number[], width: number): void

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: Sizes the pass's targets, in device pixels.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: Draws the scene with its lines into the renderer's current target, or onto the screen when it has none.

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera): void

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees its targets.

modules.title: Characters
modules.doc:
Characters: the picture drawn as text, a grid of cells over the view with one character in each. A cell's character
is picked by how much of the cell there is to show (its tone: more ink for more of it), or, where an edge runs
through the cell, by which way the edge runs: `|`, `-`, `/` or `\`. The grid is fixed on the screen, so the
characters stand in rows and columns and never slide; and a cell keeps the character it had unless another has
become clearly closer, so a cell whose tone sits between two characters does not flip back and forth as lights
flicker and the view turns.

This file is the CPU twin of the engine's pass (`GlyphPass` in splat-engine/glyphPass.ts): change one, change both.

entries.name: RAMP
entries.doc: The characters that show tone, from none to the most ink.

entries.name: STROKES
entries.doc: The characters that show an edge: upright, level (drawn as a dash the width of the cell), rising and falling.

entries.name: GLYPHS
entries.doc: Every character, in the order the engine numbers them.

entries.name: glyphBit
entries.doc: Whether a character has ink at a pixel of its cell (`x` from the left, `y` from the top).

signatures.code: glyphBit(glyph: number, x: number, y: number): boolean

entries.name: RAMP_INK
entries.doc: How much ink each character of the ramp lays down, as a share of the heaviest one's: what its tone is.

entries.name: glyphAtlas
entries.doc: The font as one strip of bytes, a character after another from the left, 255 where there is ink: what the engine samples.

signatures.code: glyphAtlas(): { width: number; height: number; data: Uint8Array }

entries.name: GlyphLook
entries.doc: How the picture is drawn as characters (`Stage.setGlyphs`).

props.name: size
props.doc: How tall a cell is in CSS pixels (default 12; a cell is three quarters as wide). It is rounded so every pixel of the font is a whole number of device pixels.

props.name: ink
props.doc: The characters' color, sRGB 0–1. Left out, each takes the color of what it stands for.

props.name: light
props.doc: For a light ground: darker things get the heavier characters. Without it (a dark ground) lighter things do.

props.name: edges
props.doc: Draw a stroke where an edge runs through a cell: where the picture ends, one thing stands in front of another, two parts meet, or the tone changes sharply (default true).

props.name: strands
props.doc:
Draw a stroke along what is long and thin on the screen, such as strands of fur and blades of grass, where a cell
is mostly that (default true). The stroke is the one of `|`, `_`, `/` and `` nearest the way they run.

props.name: steady
props.doc: How much closer another character's tone has to be before a cell gives up the one it has, 0–0.5 of the whole range (default `STICK`; 0 never keeps one).

props.name: gain
props.doc: Tones are multiplied by this before a character is picked (default 1): over 1 for a dim scene.

props.name: set
props.doc:
Which characters (default 'ascii'): 'braille' draws each cell as the braille character whose eight dots are on
where that eighth of the cell is heavy enough, and 'blocks' as the quarter blocks (▘ ▚ ▙ and so on) or, where a
cell is even, one of the shades ░ ▒ ▓. Both show shapes within a cell, so `edges` and `strands` are not used.

entries.name: GlyphSet
entries.doc: The kinds of characters a picture can be drawn in (`GlyphLook.set`).

entries.name: toneOf
entries.doc:
A cell's tone, 0–1: how heavy a character it wants. `rgb` is the mean of the picture over the cell, linear and
premultiplied, `cover` its mean alpha: a cell the subject only half fills gets a lighter character, which softens
the outline.

signatures.code: toneOf(rgb: ArrayLike<number>, cover: number, look?: GlyphLook): number

entries.name: rampFor
entries.doc:
The ramp character for a tone: the one whose ink is nearest, unless the cell had a ramp character the frame before
(`before`, its number) that is no more than `steady` further off.

signatures.code: rampFor(tone: number, before?: number, steady?: number): number

entries.name: Probe
entries.doc: What the picture is at one of a cell's probes.

props.name: shown
props.doc: Whether anything is drawn there.

props.name: tone
props.doc: Its tone there (`toneOf` of that one point).

props.name: depth
props.doc: How far in front of the camera it is.

props.name: part
props.doc: Which part it is, as any number that differs between parts.

entries.name: strokeFor
entries.doc:
The stroke for a cell, as a number in `GLYPHS`, or -1 for none. The probes are left, right, above, below, then
above left, above right, below left and below right of the cell's middle. An edge runs along the one way in which
both ends are on the same side while the way across it is not: upright and level are tried first.

entries.name: GlyphCell
entries.doc: A cell as drawn: its character and that character's color.

props.name: glyph
props.doc: The character's number in `GLYPHS` (0 is a space).

props.name: color
props.doc: Its color, linear RGB.

entries.name: glyphCell
entries.doc:
One cell: its character and color from the picture's mean over the cell (`rgb` linear and premultiplied, `cover`
its alpha), the two rings of probes when edges are wanted (the inner eight, then the outer eight), and the character
it had the frame before (-1 for none). `ink` here is linear. `lie` is the cell's mean lie (`strandFor`) when strands
are wanted: a cell of strands takes their stroke, lit by its tone, before any edge is looked for.

signatures.code: glyphCell(rgb: ArrayLike<number>, cover: number, probes: readonly Probe[] | undefined, look?: GlyphLook, before?: number, ink?: ArrayLike<number>, lie?: ArrayLike<number>): GlyphCell

entries.name: brailleFor
entries.doc:
A braille cell's dots from the tones of its eight parts (two across, four down, a row after another from the top):
as bits from U+2800. A dot is on where its part's tone reaches its `DOT_STEP`; one that was on the frame before
(`before`, the same bits, or -1) stays on down to `steady` under it, so a dot at its step does not blink.

signatures.code: brailleFor(tones: ArrayLike<number>, before?: number, steady?: number): number

entries.name: QUADS
entries.doc: The quarter blocks, by their bits: above left 1, above right 2, below left 4, below right 8.

entries.name: SHADES
entries.doc: The shades, light to dark, numbered after the quarter blocks.

entries.name: blockFor
entries.doc:
A blocks cell from the tones of its four quarters (above left, above right, below left, below right): an even cell
is the shade nearest its mean (kept, like a ramp character, unless another is `steady` closer), and an uneven one is
the quarter block with the quarters over the middle of its tones (kept while no quarter is clearly on the other side).

signatures.code: blockFor(q: ArrayLike<number>, before?: number, steady?: number): number

entries.name: shapeCell
entries.doc:
One cell drawn in braille or blocks (`GlyphLook.set`): `parts` are the tones of its eighths or quarters (`toneOf` of
each), the rest as for `glyphCell`. The color is the cell's own at the level its heaviest part asks for.

signatures.code: shapeCell(rgb: ArrayLike<number>, cover: number, parts: ArrayLike<number>, look?: GlyphLook, before?: number, ink?: ArrayLike<number>): GlyphCell

entries.name: setBit
entries.doc: Whether a character of a set has ink at a pixel of its 6 × 8 cell (`x` from the left, `y` from the top): what the engine draws.

signatures.code: setBit(set: GlyphSet, glyph: number, x: number, y: number): boolean

entries.name: charOf
entries.doc: A character of a set as text.

entries.name: glyphText
entries.doc: A grid of characters (their numbers in `GLYPHS`, or a set's own numbers, a row after another from the top) as lines of text, with spaces at line ends dropped.

signatures.code: glyphText(glyphs: ArrayLike<number>, columns: number, set?: GlyphSet): string

entries.name: glyphScale
entries.doc: How many device pixels one pixel of the font is, for a cell `size` CSS pixels tall: whole, and at least 1.

entries.name: GlyphPass
entries.doc:
The picture as characters (splat-core/glyphs.ts is the CPU twin: change one, change both). The frame is drawn three
times with the same moved and sorted blobs, as for drawn outlines: the picture, a map of depth and a map of parts.
One small pass then decides every cell of the grid (its character and that character's color, kept in a target a
cell a pixel, beside the one from the frame before so a cell can keep its character), and a second draws the
characters from the font, each of the font's pixels a whole number of device pixels.

props.name: picture
props.doc: The picture, as the stage draws it without characters.

props.name: grid
props.doc: The grid of the frame just drawn: a pixel a cell, the character's number in alpha.

methods.name: setLook
methods.doc: The look; `ink` is linear RGB here, or left out for each character to take its own color.

signatures.code: setLook(look: GlyphLook, ink?: readonly number[]): void

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: Sizes the pass for a picture in device pixels, with `scale` of them to one pixel of the font.

signatures.code: setSize(width: number, height: number, scale: number): void

methods.name: forget
methods.doc: Forgets the frame before: for when what is being drawn is swapped for something else.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: Draws the scene as characters into the renderer's current target, or onto the screen when it has none.

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera): void

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees its targets.

entries.name: CelPass
entries.doc:
Cel shading (splat-core/cel.ts). The frame is drawn four times with the same moved and sorted blobs: the picture in
the blobs' own flat colors, a map of depth, a map of parts and a map of tones (how each blob faces the light). The
scene is also drawn once as the light sees it, as a map of depth (a shadow map), whenever the blobs or the light
have moved. One pass then finds, for each pixel, whether the light sees it; a second smooths that and the facing
over each surface, cuts them into light and shade, paints the picture with them and draws an even line round the
subject, where one thing passes in front of another, and between its parts.

The world must be drawing for it: flat marks, `cel` on, and its first light the one to shade by (`Stage.setCel` sets
all three). The frame's camera must be a perspective camera.

props.name: picture
props.doc: The picture: every blob flat in its own color.

props.name: ids
props.doc: The map of parts the lines between parts come from.

props.name: tones
props.doc: The map of tones (`SplatWorld.tones`).

props.name: shadow
props.doc: The scene's depth as the light sees it, counted from the near side of the scene.

methods.name: setLook
methods.doc: The look, and how many device pixels a CSS pixel is.

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: Sizes the pass's targets, in device pixels.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: Draws the scene cel shaded into the renderer's current target, or onto the screen when it has none.

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera): void

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees its targets.

modules.title: Cel shading: the arithmetic
modules.doc:
Cel shading: the light on a picture cut into a few flat tones with clean edges, as an animation cel is painted, in
place of light that fades smoothly round a form.

Nothing is faked on the finished picture. Each blob is drawn flat in its own color (the `flat` mark), and the engine
works out, for each blob, how it faces the light and how much of the light gets to it past what stands in the way
(`toneAt` in splat-engine/light.ts and its shader twin). Those two numbers are drawn as a picture of their own, and
smoothed a little over the surface they lie on before they are cut into tones: a blob is a disc some pixels across,
and cutting first would leave every shadow with an edge of discs.

This file is the arithmetic of the cut, the CPU twin of the engine's pass (`CelPass` in splat-engine/celPass.ts):
change one, change both.

entries.name: CelLook
entries.doc: How a picture is cel shaded (`Stage.setCel`).

props.name: from
props.doc: The way to the light, in the world (it needs no length). Default up, to the right and toward the front.

props.name: tones
props.doc: How many tones the light is cut into: 2 is light and shade, 3 adds a brighter tone where a surface faces the light squarely (default 2).

props.name: shade
props.doc: What shade multiplies a color by, sRGB 0–1: a cool violet gray by default, as shadows are painted on a cel.

props.name: bright
props.doc: How far the brightest of three tones goes toward white, 0–1 (default 0.2).

props.name: shadows
props.doc: Whether things cast shadows on one another (default true). Without them a surface is only lit by how it faces the light.

props.name: smooth
props.doc: How far the light is smoothed over a surface before it is cut into tones, in CSS pixels (default 8): more gives rounder, simpler shadow shapes.

props.name: soft
props.doc: How soft the edge between two tones is, 0–1 (default 0: as crisp as the screen's pixels allow).

props.name: line
props.doc: The outline's width in CSS pixels (default 1.5); 0 draws none.

props.name: ink
props.doc: The outline's color, sRGB 0–1 (default near black).

props.name: shadowSize
props.doc: How many pixels a side the light's view of the scene is, which cast shadows are read from (default and most 2048): fewer is cheaper to draw and gives softer shadow edges.

props.name: shadowEvery
props.doc: The light's view is drawn again at most every this many frames (default 1, every frame something moves): 2 halves its cost and leaves cast shadows a frame behind.

props.name: lamps
props.doc:
What the scene's own lights add to a color where they reach it (linear, added to what the tone multiplies it by).
Left out, a `Stage` works it out from the lights set on it (`lampTint`); black takes the lamps away.

props.name: ambient
props.doc: What both tones are multiplied by (linear), such as a night's dim blue. On a `Stage` its ambient light multiplies them too, so a scene that dims dims here.

entries.name: CEL_FROM
entries.doc: The default way to the light.

entries.name: CEL_SHADE
entries.doc: The default shade.

entries.name: CEL_INK
entries.doc: The default outline color.

entries.name: CEL_TURN
entries.doc:
A surface is in the light when it faces the light by more than this: its `facing` is half the cosine of the angle
between its normal and the way to the light, plus a half, so 0.5 is edge on. A little past edge on, as it is drawn by
hand: a surface the light only grazes reads as shade.

entries.name: CEL_BRIGHT
entries.doc: With three tones, a surface facing the light by this much or more takes the brightest.

entries.name: CEL_CAST
entries.doc: A blob is in a cast shadow when less than this share of the light gets to it.

entries.name: CEL_LAMP
entries.doc: A surface is in a lamp's light when the scene's lamps reach it by this much or more (`toneAt`'s `lamps` in splat-engine/light.ts).

entries.name: CEL_GLOWS
entries.doc: From this much, what reaches a surface is its own light (a flame, a lit pane): it is never darker than its own color.

entries.name: LAMP_ADD
entries.doc: How strong the color lamps add is, where the lights set no more: the brightest channel of `lampTint`.

entries.name: CEL_EDGE
entries.doc: The least width of a tone's edge, in the units of what is cut (facing and share of light, both 0–1), so the edge is not stepped.

entries.name: CEL_UNSURE
entries.doc: A blob with no flat side has no facing of its own; where nothing round a pixel has one, it is taken to face the light this much.

entries.name: celTones
entries.doc:
The tones at a point: `lit` is 0 in shade and 1 in the light, `bright` 1 where the third tone is. `facing` is how
the surface faces the light (0 away, 0.5 edge on, 1 toward) and `through` the share of the light that reaches it.

signatures.code: celTones(facing: number, through: number, look?: CelLook): { lit: number; bright: number }

entries.name: celColor
entries.doc:
A color (linear RGB) under the tones `celTones` gives: `shade` (linear) multiplies it in shade, and the brightest
tone goes toward white. `by` is the scene's own light: `ambient` multiplies both tones, `lamps` is added where the
scene's lamps reach (`reach`, from `toneAt`: one more tone, cut at `CEL_LAMP`), and from `CEL_GLOWS` the color is
never darker than itself.

signatures.code: celColor(rgb: ArrayLike<number>, tones: { lit: number; bright: number }, shade: ArrayLike<number>, bright?: number, by?: { reach: number; lamps?: ArrayLike<number>; ambient?: ArrayLike<number> }): [number, number, number]

entries.name: lampTint
entries.doc:
The color the scene's lamps add in cel shading (linear): the color of its point lights taken together, each by its
brightness, with its strongest channel at `LAMP_ADD`. Black where there are none.

signatures.code: lampTint(lights: readonly { color: ArrayLike<number>; position?: unknown }[]): [number, number, number]

entries.name: SHADOW_FAR
entries.doc: How many times the scene's size away the light's view of it is taken from: far enough that its shadows fall nearly side by side.

entries.name: shadowView
entries.doc:
Where to stand to see the scene as the light does, for a map of what the light reaches: a narrow view from
`SHADOW_FAR` sizes away along the way to the light, round a ball that holds the scene. The ball's middle and size
are rounded onto steps of their own, so a scene whose bounds wander as it moves keeps one view, and its shadows
keep their pixels. `fov` is in degrees.

signatures.code: shadowView(center: ArrayLike<number>, radius: number, from: ArrayLike<number>): { eye: [number, number, number]; target: [number, number, number]; up: [number, number, number]; fov: number; near: number; far: number; radius: number }

entries.name: SAME_COLOR
entries.doc: Two colors of one part nearer than this in OKLab are gathered into one: the mottle of a painted surface, not a stripe.

entries.name: gatherColors
entries.doc:
Flat fills for a cel: each part's colors gathered into a few, so a mottled or textured surface becomes areas of one
color and a stripe, a spot or a white chest stays its own. `color` holds a color a blob (sRGB, 0–1, three numbers
each) and `partOf` each blob's part (left out, the blobs are one part); a part keeps at most `most` colors, and
fewer where they are within `SAME_COLOR` of one another. The same blobs always give the same colors: the first
color of a part is its commonest, and each next the one furthest from those chosen, before a few rounds settle them.

With `round` (where each blob is, three numbers each, and how far round it to look), a blob then takes the color most
of its part's blobs within that reach have, twice over: speckle finer than the reach goes, and anything wider (a
stripe, a patch, a checker) keeps its edge.

signatures.code: gatherColors(color: ArrayLike<number>, partOf?: ArrayLike<number>, most?: number, round?: { at: ArrayLike<number>; reach: number }): Float32Array

entries.name: NeonPass
entries.doc:
Neon (splat-core/neon.ts): tubes of light along the picture's outlines, over bodies kept dark that catch the
tubes' light. The frame is drawn three times with the same moved and sorted blobs (the picture in the blobs' own
flat colors, a map of depth and a map of parts), as outlines are (inkLines.ts), and the tubes run where those
lines would: round the subject, where one thing passes in front of another, and between its parts. A tube takes
the color of the thing it goes round at full strength (`neonColor`), or one of the look's colors by its part, and
shines by where it is in the world: pulses of light run through the scene two ways (`shineAt`), so the light
travels along the tubes. The tubes' light is then spread at three sizes, and the last pass paints each body in its
own color times the light that reaches it, with the glow and the tubes over it. Whatever gives its own light
(`Actor.glow`) is a lamp: filled with its color and spread onto the bodies round it as the tubes' light is.

The world should be drawing flat marks with no light of its own and a `glowGain` of `NEON_EMIT` (`Stage.setNeon` sets all three). The frame's camera
must be a perspective camera.

props.name: picture
props.doc: The picture: every blob flat in its own color, with what gives its own light drawn over white (`NEON_EMIT`), which is how the pass knows a lamp.

props.name: ids
props.doc: The map of parts the tubes between parts come from.

methods.name: setLook
methods.doc:
The look, how many device pixels a CSS pixel is, the scene's size in the world (which the pulses are spaced by)
and the stage's time in seconds.

signatures.code: setLook(look: NeonLook, ratio: number, size: number, time: number): void

methods.doc: Sizes the pass's targets, in device pixels.
