methods.doc: Draws the scene in neon into the renderer's current target, or onto the screen when it has none.

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera): void

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees its targets.

modules.title: Neon: the arithmetic
modules.doc:
Neon (Matt's idea, 2026-11-19): a scene drawn as tubes of glowing light along its outlines, over bodies kept dark
that catch the light as it runs along the tubes. The arithmetic here is pure; `splat-engine/neonPass.ts` is its
shader twin (change both).

entries.name: NeonLook
entries.doc: How a stage draws neon (`Stage.setNeon`).

props.name: line
props.doc: How wide a tube is, in CSS pixels (2).

props.name: glow
props.doc: How strongly the tubes' light spills round them and onto the bodies: 0 none, 1 as designed, up to 2.

props.name: body
props.doc: How lit the bodies are with no tube near, as a share of their own color (`NEON_BODY`).

props.name: colors
props.doc: The tubes' colors (sRGB 0–1), dealt out part by part. Left out, each tube takes the color of the thing it goes round, at full strength.

props.name: period
props.doc: How many seconds a pulse of light takes to come round again; 0 holds the light still (4). A scene that loops wants a whole number of these in its loop.

props.name: apart
props.doc: How far apart two pulses run, as a share of the scene's size (0.45).

entries.name: NEON_BODY
entries.doc: Bodies with no tube near keep this share of their own color.

entries.name: NEON_REST
entries.doc: A tube between pulses shines this much of its full light.

entries.name: NEON_TAIL
entries.doc: How fast a pulse dies away behind its head: its light is (1 − how far behind, as a share of the way to the next) to this power.

entries.name: NEON_FLOOR
entries.doc: A tube's color keeps at least this much of each channel, so a pure red still has a hot core.

entries.name: NEON_BLACK
entries.doc: A thing darker than this in every channel (linear) has no hue to speak of, and its tube is white.

entries.name: NEON_VIVID
entries.doc: How much stronger than its own a tube's color is made, about its gray.

entries.name: NEON_EMIT
entries.doc:
How many times its own color a thing that gives its own light (`Actor.glow`: a lamp, a lit window, a flame) is
drawn into neon's picture, so the pass can tell it from a pale thing: its color goes over white (`lampShare`).

entries.name: NEON_LAMP
entries.doc: A pixel whose brightest channel is over the first of these is partly a lamp, and over the second wholly one.

entries.name: NEON_LAMP_SHINE
entries.doc: How brightly a lamp shines beside a tube at a pulse's head.

entries.name: NEON_COLORS
entries.doc: The most colors a look may deal out.

entries.name: NEON_WAYS
entries.doc: The two ways pulses run through a scene (not unit: the second set of pulses lies closer together).
entries.type: readonly [readonly [number, number, number], readonly [number, number, number]]

entries.name: NEON_SECOND
entries.doc: The second set of pulses' share of the first's light.

entries.name: NEON_SHIFT
entries.doc: How far a part's own number shifts its pulses, in pulses.

entries.name: neonColor
entries.doc:
The color of the tube round a thing of color `rgb` (linear, 0–1): the same hue at full strength, however dark the
thing is. A gray thing gets a white tube.

entries.name: pulse
entries.doc: One set of pulses: 1 at a pulse's head, dying away behind it to nothing just before the next. `phase` counts pulses.

entries.name: shineAt
entries.doc:
How brightly a tube shines at a place: `along` is the place measured along each of the two ways, in pulses (its
part's shift included), `turn` how many pulses have gone by. Never under `NEON_REST`, 1 at a head.

signatures.code: shineAt(along: readonly [number, number], turn: number): number

entries.name: lampShare
entries.doc:
How much of a pixel of neon's picture is a lamp, from its brightest channel (`top`): nothing up to white, all of
it well over. A lamp is filled with its own light, steady, and that light is spread onto the bodies round it as
the tubes' is.

entries.name: colorOf
entries.doc: Which of `count` colors a part takes, from the part's shift (0–1).

entries.name: bodyColor
entries.doc:
A body's color (linear) under the tubes' light: its own color times what it keeps unlit plus the light that
reaches it (`light`, the tubes' light spread out, linear).

signatures.code: bodyColor(own: readonly number[], light: readonly number[], body?: number, glow?: number): [number, number, number]

entries.name: GlassPass
entries.doc:
Stained glass (splat-core/glass.ts). The frame is drawn three times with the same moved and sorted blobs (the
picture in the blobs' own flat colors, a map of depth and a map of parts), as outlines are (inkLines.ts). One pass
then puts each pixel back in the world from its depth and asks which pane it is in: panes are the cells nearest a
scatter of points fixed in the world, so they stay on their surfaces as the view turns. A pane's glass is the
picture's own color there, made richer and lighter and a little different from the next pane's, with the light
behind it. Lead runs between panes, round every part, where one thing passes in front of another, round the
subject, and wherever the picture's color changes, so each piece between leads is one color: it wants blobs in
flat colors with no light baked in. Pixels the subject leaves empty are panes too, fixed on the screen and colored as the look's sky, so the
whole picture is a window.

The world should be drawing flat marks with no light of its own (`Stage.setGlass` sets both). The frame's camera must be a perspective camera.

props.name: picture
props.doc: The picture: every blob flat in its own color.

props.name: ids
props.doc: The map of parts the lead between parts comes from.

methods.name: setLook
methods.doc: The look, how many device pixels a CSS pixel is, and the scene's size in the world (which panes are sized by).

signatures.code: setLook(look: GlassLook, ratio: number, size: number): void

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: Sizes the pass's targets, in device pixels.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: Draws the scene as stained glass into the renderer's current target, or onto the screen when it has none.

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera): void

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees its targets.

modules.title: Stained glass: the arithmetic
modules.doc:
Stained glass (Matt picked it, 2026-11-19): a scene drawn as a leaded window. Every surface is cut into panes of
flat colored glass that stay on it as the view turns, with lead between the panes, round every part, wherever
the color changes and round the subject, and the light comes from behind. The arithmetic here is pure; `splat-engine/glassPass.ts` is its
shader twin (change both).

entries.name: GlassLook
entries.doc: How a stage draws stained glass (`Stage.setGlass`).

props.name: pane
props.doc: How big a pane is, as a share of the scene's size (0.06).

props.name: lead
props.doc: How wide the lead is, in CSS pixels (3).

props.name: ink
props.doc: The lead's color (sRGB 0–1).

props.name: sky
props.type: readonly [readonly [number, number, number], readonly [number, number, number]]
props.doc: The window round the subject, top and bottom (sRGB 0–1): empty pixels are panes of these. Left out, pale blue over warm white.

props.name: light
props.doc: Where the light behind the window is brightest, across and down the picture (0–1; [0.5, 0.3]).

props.name: shine
props.doc: How much brighter the glass is at the light than far from it: 0 lights the window evenly (0.5).

props.name: vary
props.doc: How much one pane's glass differs from the next's, 0 to 1 (0.5).

entries.name: GLASS_RICH
entries.doc: Glass is richer than paint: its color is made this much stronger about its gray.

entries.name: GLASS_LIFT
entries.doc: And lighter, since the light comes through it: its color is raised to this power (under 1 lightens).

entries.name: GLASS_VARY
entries.doc: One pane's glass is lighter or darker than the next's by up to this share, at full `vary`.

entries.name: GLASS_SKY_PANE
entries.doc: The window round the subject is cut into panes this many times a scene pane's size on screen, as a share of the picture's height.

entries.name: GLASS_JUMP
entries.doc: Lead also runs where the picture's own color (linear) changes by more than this from one pixel to one a lead's width away.

entries.name: GLASS_LEAD
entries.doc: The lead (sRGB 0–1): near black, a little warm.

entries.name: GLASS_SKY
entries.doc: The window with no sky of the subject's own, top and bottom (sRGB 0–1).
entries.type: readonly [readonly [number, number, number], readonly [number, number, number]]

entries.name: cellHash
entries.doc: A number from 0 to 1 for a grid cell, different for each `salt`.

signatures.code: cellHash(x: number, y: number, z: number, salt: number): number

entries.name: seedOf
entries.doc: Where a grid cell's pane has its middle: somewhere in the cell.

signatures.code: seedOf(x: number, y: number, z: number): [number, number, number]

entries.name: paneOf
entries.doc:
The pane a point is in, with panes one unit across: the grid cell whose seed is nearest (`cell`, `seed`) and how
far the point is from the nearest other pane (`edge`: its distance to the plane halfway between the two seeds).
Lead is drawn where `edge` is under half the lead's width.

signatures.code: paneOf(p: readonly number[]): { cell: [number, number, number]; seed: [number, number, number]; edge: number }

entries.name: glassColor
entries.doc: A color (linear, 0–1) as glass with the light behind it: richer and lighter.

entries.name: paneTint
entries.doc: What a pane's glass is multiplied by: each pane a little lighter or darker than the next, by its cell.

signatures.code: paneTint(cell: readonly number[], vary?: number): number

entries.name: backLight
entries.doc: How bright the light behind the window is at a place in the picture (`at` and `light` across and down, 0–1; `aspect` is width over height): 1 at the light, falling to 1 − `shine` far from it.

signatures.code: backLight(at: readonly number[], light: readonly number[], shine?: number, aspect?: number): number

entries.name: BLOCK_LIGHTS
entries.doc: How many of the stage's lights reach the blocks; the rest are dropped.

entries.name: EDGE_WIDTH
entries.doc: How far in from a face's edge its line reaches, as a share of the face.

entries.name: LAMP_WRAP
entries.doc: How much of a lamp's light a face turned away from it still takes: lamps cast no shadows here, so a little wraps round.

entries.name: BlockActor
entries.doc: What a view needs of an actor: what blocks are made from, and the posed bones that carry them.
entries.type: BlockSource & { skeleton: { matrix: Float32Array; scale: Float32Array; bones: readonly { name: string }[] } }

entries.name: BlockView
entries.doc:
A scene drawn as blocks (blocks.ts): one mesh for each bone that carries cubes, moved by that bone whole, so cubes
never bend. The look's own light is in the corners already; this adds the stage's lamps to each face by where it
is and which way it faces now, keeps a block that gives its own light at its own color, and draws a thin line
round each face. It draws into a target with four samples a pixel and copies that out, since a cube's edges want
smoothing that soft blobs never did.

ctor.code: new BlockView(actors: readonly BlockActor[], look: BlockLook)

props.name: blocks
props.doc: How many cubes it holds.

props.name: faces
props.doc: How many faces of them it draws: those with no cube of the same bone beside them.

methods.name: setLights
methods.doc: The stage's lights and ambient light, as `SplatWorld.setLights` takes them; `tint` multiplies the ambient (a night's light).

signatures.code: setLights(lights: readonly Light[], ambient?: number | readonly [number, number, number], tint?: readonly [number, number, number]): void

methods.name: pose
methods.doc: Puts every piece where its bone is now.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: Draws the scene (this view in it) into the renderer's current target, or onto the screen when it has none, with its edges smoothed.

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera, width: number, height: number): void

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees the meshes and the target.

entries.name: BlockLook
entries.doc:
Blocks: a scene's blobs snapped onto a grid and drawn as cubes (`Stage.setBlocks`). Every grid cell that holds a
blob becomes one cube in the commonest color among its blobs, on the bone most of them ride, so a scene still
moves: its still parts stay on the grid and a moving part carries its cubes with it. The light is worked out here,
once, for the rest pose: each face is flat in one tone by which way it faces the light, a face something stands
in front of is in shade as a whole, and corners where blocks meet are a little darker. That wants blobs with no
light baked into them. This file is the arithmetic (pure, tested); blockView.ts draws it.

props.name: cell
props.doc: A block's side, in the blobs' units: the grid a scene was cut on, or a whole number of it for bigger blocks.

props.name: from
props.doc: The way to the light (any length; default up, right and toward the front).

props.name: shade
props.doc: How much light a face in shade keeps, 0 to 1 (default 0.45).

props.name: shadows
props.doc: Whether blocks cast shadows on the faces behind them (default true).

props.name: corners
props.doc: How much darker a face gets in a corner where blocks meet, 0 to 1 (default 0.5).

props.name: vary
props.doc: How much one block's color differs from the next's, 0 to 1 (default 0.35).

props.name: edge
props.doc: How dark the line round each face is, 0 to 1 (default 0.3); 0 for none.

props.name: ambient
props.doc: What the stage's ambient light is multiplied by, linear (a night's dim blue; default none).

props.name: least
props.doc: Blobs fainter than this are left out (mist, haze; default 0.3).

entries.name: BLOCK_FROM
entries.doc: The default way to the light.

entries.name: BLOCK_SHADE
entries.doc: The default light a face in shade keeps.

entries.name: CORNER_MOST
entries.doc: How much of its light a face loses with all of a corner shut in, at `corners` 1.

entries.name: VARY_MOST
entries.doc: How far a block's lightness is from its color's own at most, at `vary` 1.

entries.name: SKY_SHARE
entries.doc: A face in shade is this much darker again when it faces straight down, and as much lighter facing up.

entries.name: SPECK_SIZE
entries.doc:
Loose things in the air (rain, sparks, fireflies: bones whose names start with `~`) are cubes this share of a block
across, on a grid of their own, and take no part in shadows or corners.

entries.name: GLOW_CLEAR
entries.doc: A block that gives this much of its own light or more (the mean of its blobs' `glow`) casts no shadow.

entries.name: BlockSource
entries.doc: What blocks are made from: an actor's blobs, its skin, the names of its bones and the light its blobs give.

props.name: blobs
props.doc: The blobs in the rest pose.

props.name: skin
props.doc: Which bones move each blob: a block rides the bone most of its blobs do.

props.name: skeleton
props.doc: The bones, for their names: one whose name starts with `~` carries loose specks.

props.name: glow
props.doc: How much of its own light each blob gives, a byte a blob (`Actor.glow`).

entries.name: BlockPiece
entries.doc: The cubes on one bone of one actor, as a mesh: four corners a face, two triangles.

props.name: actor
props.doc: Which of the sources it came from.

props.name: bone
props.doc: Which of that source's bones carries it.

props.name: blocks
props.doc: How many cubes.

props.name: positions
props.doc: Corner places in the rest pose, three numbers each.

props.name: normals
props.doc: Each corner's face normal.

props.name: colors
props.doc: Each corner's color, linear, the block's own with no light on it.

props.name: light
props.doc: Three numbers a corner: the light its face has from the look's light (shade and shadow in), what is left of any light in its corner, and how much of its own light the block gives.

props.name: uvs
props.doc: Each corner's place on its face, 0 or 1 each way.

props.name: indices
props.doc: Three corners a triangle.

entries.name: blockHash
entries.doc: A number from 0 to 1 for a cell, the same each time.

signatures.code: blockHash(x: number, y: number, z: number): number

entries.name: faceLight
entries.doc:
How much of the look's light each of a cube's six faces has when nothing is in the way, 0 to 1, in the order
+x, -x, +y, -y, +z, -z: by how squarely it faces the light, with the face that faces it most at 1, so no two of
the three faces a view shows are alike unless the light lies evenly between them.

entries.name: faceTone
entries.doc: The light a face has: its shade (a little more of it facing the sky, less facing the ground) and its share of the light where that reaches it.

signatures.code: faceTone(face: number, lit: number, shade: number, sun: readonly number[]): number

entries.name: faceLit
entries.doc:
Whether the look's light reaches the face `face` of the cell at x, y, z: a walk from the face's middle toward the
light, half a cell at a time, until a solid cell is met or the walk is out of the box that holds them all.

signatures.code: faceLit(solid: (x: number, y: number, z: number) => boolean, x: number, y: number, z: number, face: number, from: readonly [number, number, number], lo: readonly number[], hi: readonly number[]): boolean

entries.name: buildBlocks
entries.doc:
The sources as blocks: a mesh for each bone that carries any (see `BlockLook`). A cell two bones' blobs share goes
to the bone with more of them, so no two cubes ever stand in one place; faces between two cubes on one bone are
left out. Shadows and corners are worked out within each source, never from one to another.

signatures.code: buildBlocks(sources: readonly BlockSource[], look: BlockLook): { pieces: BlockPiece[]; blocks: number; faces: number }

entries.name: GlitchLook
entries.doc: What the page's controls make.

props.name: amount
props.doc: How often a burst comes, 0 (never) to 1 (most of the time).

props.name: strength
props.doc: How hard a burst is, 0 to 1: how far rows slide, channels split and how many blocks go.

props.name: jitter
props.doc: A burst slides bands of rows sideways.

props.name: split
props.doc: A burst reads red to one side and blue to the other.

props.name: blocks
props.doc: A burst takes blocks of the art from somewhere else.

props.name: pace
props.doc: Steps a second: a burst changes this often, never in between.

props.name: loop
props.doc: The scene's loop in seconds, where it has one: steps and bursts repeat with it.

props.name: still
props.doc: Under reduced motion: no bursts at all (a flicker is exactly what that asks to be spared).

props.name: seed
props.doc: Picks another run of bursts.

entries.name: GlitchState
entries.doc: One step's glitch, in art pixels: what the pass is handed each frame. All whole numbers.

props.name: on
props.doc: A burst is on.

props.name: key
props.doc: The step's own number for `glitchHash`, under 2^24.

props.name: jitter
props.doc: Most a row band slides either way, in art pixels (0: no jitter).

props.name: band
props.doc: Rows to a band.

props.name: rows
props.doc: The share of bands that slide, as a threshold over 2^24.

props.name: split
props.doc: How far red and blue are read to each side (0: no split).

props.name: block
props.doc: A corrupted block's height in art pixels (it is `BLOCK_WIDE` times as wide).

props.name: blocks
props.doc: The share of blocks corrupted, as a threshold over 2^24 (0: none).

entries.name: RUN_MOST
entries.doc: A burst lasts this many steps at most.

entries.name: START_MOST
entries.doc: The share of steps a burst starts on at `amount` 1.

entries.name: JITTER_MOST
entries.doc: At full strength, how far a band of rows slides either way.

entries.name: SPLIT_MOST
entries.doc: At full strength, how far red and blue are read to each side.

entries.name: BLOCKS_MOST
entries.doc: At full strength, the share of blocks corrupted.

entries.name: GLITCH_PACES
entries.doc: Steps a second the page offers.

entries.name: MIX_A
entries.doc: Two primes under 2^31 that spread a cell's two numbers before the hash.

entries.name: MIX_B
entries.doc: Two primes under 2^31 that spread a cell's two numbers before the hash.

entries.name: SALT
entries.doc: The salts that keep a cell's draws apart: each is one question about a row band or a block.
entries.type: { slides: 1; slide: 2; broken: 3; fromX: 4; fromY: 5; turned: 6; strip: 7 }

entries.name: STRIPS
entries.doc: Broken blocks gather in strips: this share of rows of blocks can break at all (a threshold over 2^24).

entries.name: BLOCK_WIDE
entries.doc: A broken block is this many times as wide as it is high, as a torn line of a picture is.

entries.name: TURNED
entries.doc: The share of broken blocks whose channels are turned (a threshold over 2^24).

entries.name: glitchHash
entries.doc:
The 24-bit hash of a row band or block (`a`, `b`, whole and not negative) for one question (`salt`) in the step
`key`: the GPU's `glitchHash` in pixelPass.ts, in the same unsigned 32-bit steps.

signatures.code: glitchHash(a: number, b: number, key: number, salt: number): number

entries.name: pickOf
entries.doc: A whole number from 0 to `m` − 1 out of a 24-bit hash, exact on both sides: (h · m) >> 24.

entries.name: stepsIn
entries.doc: How many steps a loop of `loop` seconds holds at `pace` a second: whole, and at least one.

entries.name: stepAt
entries.doc: The step a moment falls in, and how many steps go round (0 where nothing loops).

signatures.code: stepAt(t: number, look: GlitchLook): { k: number; n: number }

entries.name: glitchAt
entries.doc: The glitch at a moment: whether a burst is on and, if so, how it reads the art this step.

entries.name: readFrom
entries.doc:
Where the art pixel at column `x`, row `y` (from the top) reads from, in a picture `w` wide and `h` high:
`x` for green, red `split` to the right of it and blue `split` to the left, and whether its channels are turned.

signatures.code: readFrom(x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number, g: GlitchState): { x: number; y: number; turned: boolean }

entries.name: wrapX
entries.doc: A column slid off one side comes in at the other.

entries.name: glitchArt
entries.doc:
The finished art with this step's glitch laid on: the CPU twin of the live pass's last step (pixelPass.ts
`toScreen`). Off, it is the art itself.

entries.name: WashPass
entries.doc:
Watercolor (splat-core/wash.ts). The frame is drawn three times with the same moved and sorted blobs (the picture
in the blobs' own flat colors, and for the pencil a map of depth and a map of parts). The picture is softened at
half and at a quarter of its size, and one pass paints the paper: each pixel reads the softened picture a little
to one side (the paper's own wander, fixed on the screen, so a wash's edge runs unevenly), takes its color as
pigment, and lays it on the paper as see-through paint (`washed`): thinner and thicker from place to place,
gathered into the paper's grain, darker where the wash ends or its color changes (the softened picture against
the more softened one), and not at all where the picture is lightest. A look's sky is a wash behind the subject
that stops short of the paper's edge; a faint pencil line runs where outlines would.

The world should be drawing flat marks (`Stage.setWash` sets them).

props.name: picture
props.doc: The picture: every blob flat in its own color.

props.name: ids
props.doc: The map of parts the pencil's lines between parts come from.

methods.name: setLook
methods.doc: The look, and how many device pixels a CSS pixel is.

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: Sizes the pass's targets, in device pixels.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: Draws the scene in watercolor into the renderer's current target, or onto the screen when it has none.

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera): void

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees its targets.

modules.title: Watercolor: the arithmetic

entries.name: WashLook
entries.doc: How a stage draws watercolor (`Stage.setWash`).

props.name: bleed
props.doc: How far a wash's edge runs and wanders, in CSS pixels (4).

props.name: pool
props.doc: How much darker a wash dries at its edges, 0 to 1 (0.6).

modules.title: Cloth solver
modules.doc:
A small position-based dynamics solver (XPBD, "small steps" form: many
substeps, one pass over the constraints in each), for cloth and hair hung
on a rig. Points carry an inverse mass (0 = pinned, moved by the caller);
links keep two points at a length, goals pull a point toward where the
animation puts it, and capsules push points out of the body. Compliance is
the inverse of stiffness: 0 is rigid.

It always steps by `STEP`, carrying what's left of a frame to the next, so
the same frames give the same motion and a recorded loop can be played back.
Pure and tested.

modules.title: Water that ripples
modules.doc:
Still water that moves when something moves through it: a pond as a grid of heights stepped by the wave equation,
and the blobs that draw its surface.

`Water` is the pond itself, in plain numbers so it runs in Node tests. Each wet cell holds how far its surface stands
above the level and how fast it is rising. A fixed tick moves every cell toward the mean of its neighbors, which is
what makes a ring travel outward at `speed`; a dry cell gives its neighbor back its own height, so rings bounce off
banks, steps and pillars. Nothing draws rings: a body that enters, leaves or wades through the water (`body`) pushes
the water it displaces to the cells round it, and the rings are what the grid does with that.

`makeSurface` lays flat blobs over the wet cells, `shapeSurface` lifts and tilts each to the water under it, and
`shadeSurface` colors each from the view: clear looking straight down, a mirror of the sky at a low angle
(Fresnel), with a glint where it throws the sun or a lamp at the eye.

The water's energy per wet cell, 0 at rest: its motion (speed squared) plus its tilt (the squared slope between
neighbors, times the wave speed squared), which trade places as a wave passes. Waves keep it, damping spends it,
and nothing but a body or a drop adds to it.

methods.doc: The surface's slope at (x, z): how much it rises per meter along x and along z. A dry neighbor counts as level with the cell, as it does to the waves.

methods.name: body
methods.doc:
Tells the water where a body crosses its surface now (`at`, from `crossing`; null when it is out of the water or
wholly under it). `draft` is how deep the body stands in the water there, meters: a leg on the bed takes the place
of the whole column, so its draft is the water's depth. Where the body newly stands, the water it takes the place
of (a disc of its radius, `draft` deep, whatever the grid) is pressed out and put on the cells just round it;
where it stood, the water comes back the same way. So stepping in raises a ring, wading pushes a wave ahead and
leaves a trough behind, and stepping out lets the water fall back in. `id` names the body from call to call.

methods.name: rest
methods.doc: Lays the water flat and still at once, keeping what it knows of the bodies in it: for the start of a scene, where whoever stands in the pond has always stood there.

methods.name: forget
methods.doc: Forgets every body, as when the scene is set again: the next `body` call for each is a fresh entry.

methods.name: drop
methods.doc: Lets a drop of `volume` cubic meters fall at (x, z), spread over a radius `r`: a raindrop, a pebble, a tap. Nothing if it lands on dry ground.

signatures.code: drop(x: number, z: number, r: number, volume: number): void

methods.name: splash
methods.doc:
The mark a small fast thing leaves where it hits: a crater `depth` meters deep and about `r` across with a raised
rim, holding no water of its own (what the middle loses the rim gains). A raindrop is far smaller than a cell of
the grid, but its splash is not; rain given as `drop`s of that size would fill the pond. Nothing on dry ground.

signatures.code: splash(x: number, z: number, r: number, depth: number): void

methods.name: step
methods.doc: Moves the water on by `dt` seconds, in whole ticks (what is left of a frame is carried to the next).

entries.name: WaterSurface
entries.doc: The blobs that draw a pond's surface, from `makeSurface`.

props.name: at
props.doc: Where each blob lies on the pond: x then z, a pair a blob.

props.name: size
props.doc: Each blob's size at rest, across the surface.

props.name: slope
props.doc: The surface's slope under each blob as `shapeSurface` last found it: along x then along z, a pair a blob.

props.name: curve
props.doc: The surface's curvature under each blob as `shapeSurface` last found it: the sum of its second derivatives along x and z, per meter (under zero at a crest).

entries.name: WaterLook
entries.doc: How a pond's surface looks, for `shadeSurface`. Colors are linear RGB, 0 to 1.

props.name: body
props.doc: The water's own color, seen looking straight down into it.

props.name: sky
props.doc: What the surface mirrors: the sky overhead, or the dark over a night scene.

props.name: horizon
props.doc: The sky low down, where it is lighter: a ripple tips the mirror between the two, which is most of how one is seen. The same as `sky` when left out.

props.name: clear
props.doc: How solid it is looking straight down, 0 to 1: the rest of the way to 1 comes with the angle.

props.name: sun
props.type: { toward: Vec3; color: Vec3; glow?: number }
props.doc: The way to the sun (or moon), and its color: the surface glints where it throws it at the eye. `glow` is the share of that color the sky round it holds, fading over about a sixth of the sky; none when left out.

props.name: gloss
props.doc: How tight a glint is: 120 when left out. Lower spreads it into a sheen.

props.name: mirror
props.doc:
What the surface mirrors of the scene round it: a picture from `SplatMirror` for this pond's level. Where the
picture shows something, the surface mirrors that and not the sky; a ripple tips the mirrored line of sight,
so reflections wobble and break up. Left out, it mirrors the sky alone.

props.name: reach
props.doc: How far off the things mirrored are taken to stand, meters, when a ripple tips the line of sight: farther makes reflections wobble more. 1.5 when left out.

props.name: steep
props.doc: How many times steeper than it is the surface is drawn and lit, so ripples a few millimeters high read from across a scene: 1 when left out.

props.name: deep
props.doc:
How deep the water is taken to be, meters, for the light its surface gathers: a crest is a lens that draws the
light passing down through it together on the bed and a trough spreads it, so the water's own color is brighter
under crests and darker under troughs. It is what shows a ripple from above, where the surface mirrors almost
nothing. `steep` counts here too. None when left out.

entries.name: makeSurface
entries.doc:
Flat blobs over every wet cell of a pond, `per` to a cell (2 when left out), on one still bone: the surface that
`shapeSurface` moves and `shadeSurface` colors. The count never changes afterward.

signatures.code: makeSurface(water: Water, options?: { per?: number; seed?: number }): WaterSurface

entries.name: shapeSurface
entries.doc: Lifts each blob of a surface to the water under it and tilts it to the water's slope there. Call after the water moved, then hand the surface to `SplatWorld.reshape`.

signatures.code: shapeSurface(s: WaterSurface, water: Water, steep?: number): void

entries.name: GATHER_LEAST
entries.doc: The least and most light a ripple leaves or gathers on the bed, as a share of flat water's: past these the rays have crossed, and the thin-lens sum no longer holds.

entries.name: GATHER_MOST
entries.doc: The least and most light a ripple leaves or gathers on the bed, as a share of flat water's: past these the rays have crossed, and the thin-lens sum no longer holds.

entries.name: gathered
entries.doc:
How much light reaches the bed under a point of the surface, as a share of what flat water lets through, from the
surface's curvature there (the sum of its second derivatives, per meter: under zero at a crest). Light from above
bends toward the normal by (n − 1) / n of its tilt (a quarter, for water), so a patch of surface lights a patch of
bed 1 + deep · curvature / 4 times as wide each way together. 1 for a look with no `deep`.

entries.name: surfaceColor
entries.doc:
What a point of the surface sends to an eye: its color (linear) and how solid it is. Clear and its own color seen
from above, more of a mirror of the sky the lower the angle (Schlick's Fresnel for water), plus a glint where the
mirrored line of sight runs at the sun or at a lamp. Pure, so tests can ask it.

signatures.code: surfaceColor(p: Vec3, normal: Vec3, eye: ArrayLike<number>, look: WaterLook, lights?: readonly PointLight[]): { color: Vec3; opacity: number }

entries.name: shadeSurface
entries.doc:
Colors every blob of a surface for an eye at `eye` (`surfaceColor`), on the slopes `shapeSurface` last left. Call
when the water (after `shapeSurface`) or the view moved, then hand the surface to `SplatWorld.reshape` or `recolor`.

signatures.code: shadeSurface(s: WaterSurface, look: WaterLook, eye: ArrayLike<number>, lights?: readonly PointLight[]): void

entries.name: PickHit
entries.doc:
Picking: which blob of which actor is under a pointer, as the actor stands
posed right now, and which bone and part it belongs to.

Each blob's bones move it by a blend of their skin matrices. That blend, M,
carries the blob's rest ellipsoid to where it is drawn (exactly, in the
'linear' rule; to within the rounding of a joint in 'quat'), and a straight
line through M is still a straight line with the same distances along it.
So the ray is taken back into the blob's rest frame through M⁻¹ and tested
against the rest blob there, with `rayHit`, as a still scene is.

props.name: actor
props.doc: Index into the actors given.

props.name: blob
props.doc: The blob's index in that actor.

props.name: t
props.doc: Distance along the ray (in units of the direction's length).

props.name: point
props.doc: Where the ray meets the blob, in world space.

props.name: bone
props.doc: The bone that holds most of the blob.

props.name: part
props.doc: Its part (`Actor.partOf`), or 0 when the actor has none.

entries.name: PickOptions
entries.doc: Options for `pickActors`.

props.name: k
props.doc: How far out a blob counts, in standard deviations (2 is about where it fades to nothing).

props.name: minOpacity
props.doc: Blobs fainter than this are looked through.

entries.name: pickActors
entries.doc: The nearest blob a ray hits among posed actors, or null. Call each skeleton's `update()` first.

signatures.code: pickActors(actors: readonly Actor[], origin: ArrayLike<number>, dir: ArrayLike<number>, options?: PickOptions): PickHit | null

entries.name: boneShare
entries.doc: How much of each blob of an actor moves with `bone`: its weight on that bone, 0–1.

entries.name: boneLabel
entries.doc: A bone's name for people: 'lForearm' → 'left forearm', 'flUpper' → 'front left upper', 'tail3' → 'tail 3'.

modules.title: Level of detail
modules.doc:
Level of detail per actor: a creature far away or small on screen draws a
share of its blobs, each grown to cover for the ones left out, so it costs
less to draw and looks about the same.

Which blobs stay is fixed per blob by `lodRank` (a hash of its index), so a
creature thinning out loses the same blobs every time and keeps the rest:
nothing flickers as the share drifts. A kept blob's covariance is divided by
the share kept (each axis grows by 1/√keep), so the covered area stays about
the same for the surface discs creatures are cut from.

The GPU (`deformBlob` in engine.ts) and the CPU twin (`SplatWorld.deformCPU`)
use the same hash; change both.

entries.name: lodRank
entries.doc: A blob's place in line for being dropped, 0–1: blobs ranked below the share dropped are left out. Wang's integer hash.

entries.name: DetailRule
entries.doc: How many of its blobs an actor keeps for the size it is on screen.

props.name: density
props.doc:
Blobs wanted per pixel of the disc round the actor on screen. The disc is a loose fit (a long creature seen end on
fills a third of it), about half the blobs face away, and blobs overlap, so one per disc pixel still looks whole.

props.name: min
props.doc: Never fewer than this share of the blobs.

entries.name: DETAIL
entries.doc: The rule to give `world.autoDetail`: about one blob per pixel, and never under 6% of them.

entries.name: detailFor
entries.doc: The share of an actor's `count` blobs to draw when it covers a disc `radiusPx` pixels across on screen.

signatures.code: detailFor(count: number, radiusPx: number, options?: DetailRule): number

entries.name: screenRadius
entries.doc:
How many pixels a sphere of `radius` reaches on screen, `depth` units in front of a perspective camera whose
projection matrix has `p11` as its [1][1] (y focal) term, drawn `height` pixels tall. Behind the camera it is huge.

signatures.code: screenRadius(radius: number, depth: number, p11: number, height: number): number

modules.title: Cuts and paint
modules.doc:
Shape edits: cut or paint every blob inside a sphere or a box, live, without
rebuilding anything. The GPU applies them as it moves the blobs (a cut blob
gets no size, as level of detail leaves one out) and as it colors them (a
painted blob's own color is mixed toward the paint before any light).
Edits are tested against where a blob is now, in world space, so a box
that cuts a creature's head off keeps cutting as the head moves through it.

This file is the CPU twin (`editAt`), also used to bake edits into blobs for
a file (`bakeEdits`). The GPU side is `editsAt` in engine.ts; change both.

A cut can also have a clean edge (a world made with `cleanCuts`): a blob the
edge passes through is kept, and each of its pixels is tested on its own,
at the point of the blob that pixel shows most of (`densestAlong`). A file
still gets whole blobs: `bakeEdits` keeps or drops each by its center.

entries.name: ShapeEdit
entries.doc: One edit for `setEdits`: a sphere, a box or an upright cylinder in world space that cuts blobs away or paints them.

props.name: shape
props.doc: The shape of what it acts on.

props.name: center
props.doc: World position of the shape's middle.

props.name: size
props.doc: A sphere's radius (the first value), a box's half sizes, or a cylinder's radius and half height (it stands along y).

props.name: op
props.doc: Cut the blobs away, or paint them.

props.name: outside
props.doc: Act on what's outside the shape instead: a cut that keeps only the inside is a crop.

props.name: color
props.doc: Paint: the color, in sRGB 0–1 like a blob's own.

props.name: amount
props.doc: Paint: how far toward the color, 0–1 (default 1).

props.name: soft
props.doc: Paint: how far in from the edge it takes to reach full strength, in units (default 0, a hard edge).

entries.name: MAX_EDITS
entries.doc: How many edits the GPU takes at once; the rest are dropped.

entries.name: shapeDistance
entries.doc: Signed distance from p to the shape: negative inside.

entries.name: CLEAN_MARGIN
entries.doc: Clean cuts: a blob is dropped whole only when its center is this many of its sizes (`blobReach`) inside a cut.

entries.name: blobReach
entries.doc: A blob's size for clean cuts: the root of its covariance's trace (xx, xy, xz, yy, yz, zz), at least its longest standard deviation.

entries.name: densestAlong
entries.doc:
How far along a ray (`from` + t·`dir`) a blob is densest: the point of the blob a pixel on that ray shows most of.
For a flat blob that is where the ray meets its plane. `cov` is xx, xy, xz, yy, yz, zz. A blob seen edge-on, or a
needle, has no such point to speak of and gives the point of the ray nearest its center.

signatures.code: densestAlong(from: ArrayLike<number>, dir: ArrayLike<number>, center: ArrayLike<number>, cov: ArrayLike<number>): number

entries.name: editAt
entries.doc:
What the edits do to a blob at p: whether it stays, and the paint mixed over its color (linear RGB and amount).
`margin` is how far inside a cut it must be to go (0 for a point; clean cuts pass `CLEAN_MARGIN` blob sizes).

signatures.code: editAt(edits: readonly ShapeEdit[], p: ArrayLike<number>, margin?: number): { keep: boolean; paint: [number, number, number]; amount: number }

entries.name: bakeEdits
entries.doc: A copy of still blobs with the edits applied: cut blobs left out, painted ones recolored.

signatures.code: bakeEdits(b: Blobs, edits: readonly ShapeEdit[]): Blobs

entries.name: SplatDepth
entries.doc:
A depth map of a scene drawn by the engine, for post effects (fog, outlines,
focus): every pixel's distance in front of the camera, in scene units, in
all three channels of a half-float target, and 0 where nothing was drawn.
The target also carries a depth texture, for passes that want the usual
kind (ordinary meshes write it; blobs, being see-through, do not).

Splats have no single depth: a blob fades out from its middle. Here each
blob counts as a hard disc out to where it has faded to a sixth (as in the
map of parts), and the frame's own sort leaves the nearest disc on top. So
draw it right after the frame's own render, with the same camera: it reuses
that frame's moved and sorted blobs (`SplatWorld.hold`) and costs one more
draw, nothing more.

Ordinary meshes draw their own depth with a stand-in material; lines and
points (grids, helpers) are left out.

props.name: target
props.doc: The depth map: each pixel's distance in front of the camera, 0 where nothing is.

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: Sizes the map, in pixels.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: Draws the depth map of `scene` as just rendered from `camera` into `target` (sized to match the frame first).

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera): void

methods.name: read
methods.doc: For tests and tools: the map read back, one depth a pixel, rows from the top.

signatures.code: read(renderer: WebGPURenderer): Promise<{ width: number; height: number; depth: Float32Array }>

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees its render target.

modules.title: Mirrors: the arithmetic
modules.doc:
A flat mirror, and what is seen in it: the plain arithmetic of a planar reflection, apart from any drawing.

The world seen in a mirror is the world itself, flipped through the mirror's plane, seen from where the eye
really stands. So `SplatMirror` (mirror.ts) draws the scene once more with every point flipped (`mirrorMatrix`),
leaving out what lies behind the mirror, and keeps the picture with the camera it belongs to (`MirrorImage`).
A point of the mirror's surface then finds what it reflects by asking that picture (`seenIn`) where its
mirrored line of sight lands: for a flat mirror that is the very pixel the surface point itself is drawn at, and
for a rippled one (water) the line is tipped by the ripple first, which is what makes reflections wobble.

entries.name: MirrorPlane
entries.doc: A plane: the points p with normal·p + offset = 0. `normal` is one long and points out of the mirror's face.

props.name: normal
props.doc: The way the mirror faces, one long.

props.name: offset
props.doc: Minus how far the plane is from the origin along the normal.

entries.name: levelPlane
entries.doc: A level mirror at height y, facing up: a pond.

entries.name: inFront
entries.doc: How far `p` stands in front of the plane (negative behind it).

entries.name: reflectPoint
entries.doc: `p` flipped through the plane: where it is seen in the mirror.

entries.name: mirrorMatrix
entries.doc: The matrix that flips every point through the plane, 16 numbers by columns (as three.js keeps a Matrix4). It is its own inverse.

entries.name: MirrorImage
entries.doc: A picture of the mirrored world, with the camera it was drawn for.

props.name: width
props.doc: Pixels across.

props.name: height
props.doc: Pixels down.

props.name: pixels
props.doc: Red, green, blue (linear, multiplied by cover) and cover, four numbers a pixel, rows from the top. Cover is 0 where the mirror shows nothing but sky.

props.name: viewProj
props.doc: The eye's own projection times view matrix when the picture was drawn, 16 numbers by columns: where a point of the mirrored world lands in the picture.

props.name: plane
props.doc: The mirror.

entries.name: seenIn
entries.doc:
What the picture shows where the world point (x, y, z) is seen in the mirror: writes red, green, blue (times
cover) and cover into `out` and returns true, or returns false (and writes zeros) when the point is behind the
eye or off the picture. Blended between the four pixels round it.

signatures.code: seenIn(img: MirrorImage, x: number, y: number, z: number, out: number[] | Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike> | Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>): boolean

modules.title: Mirrors: what a flat mirror shows

entries.name: SplatMirror
entries.doc:
What a flat mirror shows of a scene drawn by the engine: the scene drawn once more as its mirror image, from the
same eye, into a target of its own. Water, a polished floor or a looking glass then reads it (`read`, then
`seenIn` in reflect.ts) to color itself, so whatever stands, moves or burns in the scene is in the reflection,
with nothing set up per scene.

Draw it before the frame's own render, with the frame's camera. The mirrored view puts the blobs in another
order than the frame's, so it costs a sort and a draw of its own (at the target's size, which can be small: a
rippled surface blurs what it mirrors anyway). Blobs whose centers are under the mirror, or within `lift` over
it, are left out through `SplatWorld.clip`: the bed of a pond is not in its reflection, and neither are the
blobs of the water's own surface. Lines and points are left out; ordinary meshes are drawn, but show their back
faces (a mirror image turns triangles round).

props.name: target
props.doc: The mirrored picture: linear color times cover, and cover.

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: Sizes the picture, in pixels.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: Draws `scene` as the mirror `plane` shows it to `camera`, leaving out blobs less than `lift` in front of the plane.

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera, plane: MirrorPlane, lift?: number): void

methods.name: read
methods.doc:
The picture last drawn, read back for `seenIn`, with the camera it was drawn for. Reading takes a frame or
two; while one read is under way another returns null, so call it every frame and keep the last picture.

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees its render target.

modules.title: A lens: glow and focus blur

entries.name: SplatLens
entries.doc:
A lens in front of a stage: light that spills round bright things, and blur for whatever is nearer or farther
than the distance in focus. Both come from what the frame holds, nothing is placed by hand: the glow is the
picture's own light over a knee, spread out, so a flame glows and a pale wall does not; the blur is the thin
lens's circle of confusion for each pixel's depth (`SplatDepth`), so it follows the view and the scene as they
move. The numbers are `splat-core/optics.ts` (`blurRadius`, `glowShare`), the CPU twins of the shader here:
change both.

The frame is drawn twice with one sort (the picture into a half-float target, so light over 1 is kept, then the
map of depth), and a few small passes follow: the light over the knee at half size, blurred there (the tight
halo) and again at quarter size (the wide one); then one pass over the picture that looks at each pixel through
`TAPS` points of the opening, spread as wide as the pixel's own blur or that of something nearer beside it. A point's color counts for a pixel when its own blur reaches it; something sharp
in front is not smeared by what is blurred behind it, since a point behind counts no further than the pixel's
own blur.

props.name: picture
props.doc: The picture, as the stage draws it without the lens.

methods.name: setLook
methods.doc: The lens, for a view `fov` degrees tall.

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: Sizes the pass's targets, in device pixels.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: Draws the scene through the lens into the renderer's current target, or onto the screen when it has none.

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera): void

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees its targets.

modules.title: A lens: the arithmetic
modules.doc:
A camera's lens, in plain numbers: how far out of focus a thing at some distance is, and how much of a bright
light spills round it. `SplatLens` (splat-engine/lens.ts) draws with these; they are here apart from any
drawing so tests can ask them, and so the shader and the numbers shown on a page come from one place.

Focus is the thin lens: a lens of focal length f, set to be sharp at distance s, draws a point at distance d as a
disc (its circle of confusion) of diameter A·f·|d − s| / (d·(s − f)) on the film, where A = f / N is the opening
for f-number N. So blur grows with the opening, grows fast for things nearer than the focus, and levels off behind
it. The focal length follows from the view's angle and the film's height, taken as a 35 mm frame's 24 mm unless
given: a scene a few meters across then blurs as a photograph of a small real place does.

entries.name: OpticsLook
entries.doc: How a view is finished through a lens. Distances are in the scene's units (meters).

props.name: focus
props.doc: The distance in front of the camera that is sharp.

props.name: fNumber
props.doc: The f-number: 2 is a wide opening and a thin slice in focus, 16 keeps nearly everything sharp. 0 or less turns focus blur off.

props.name: film
props.doc:
The film's height, in the scene's units: 0.024 (a 35 mm frame) when left out. A bigger film blurs more at the
same f-number. A scene photographed as a model of itself, 1/n of its size, is the same as a film n times as high.

props.name: most
props.doc: The widest blur drawn, as a share of the picture's height: 0.02 when left out.

props.name: glow
props.doc:
How strongly the light over `knee` spills round it: 0 for none. A small bright thing's light is spread thin, so
about 1 suits a picture that holds light well over white, and several one that stops at white (where a flame is
drawn no brighter than paper).

props.name: knee
props.doc: How bright (linear, 0 to 1 and over) a pixel must be before it glows: 0.7 when left out.

props.name: shoulder
props.doc:
Where strong light starts to roll off toward white instead of running straight into it, as film does: about 0.7.
Left out, light over 1 clips, each of red, green and blue on its own, which turns a fair thing in strong light
into a flat pale patch.

entries.name: focalLength
entries.doc: A lens's focal length for a view `fov` degrees tall on film `film` high, in the film's units.

entries.name: blurScale
entries.doc:
The number the shader multiplies |d − s| / d by to get a blur radius in pixels: A·f / (s − f), halved (a radius),
as a share of the film and so of the picture's `height` in pixels. 0 when focus blur is off or the focus is
inside the lens.

signatures.code: blurScale(look: OpticsLook, fov: number, height: number): number

entries.name: blurRadius
entries.doc: The radius, in pixels, of the disc a point `depth` in front of the camera is drawn as, for a picture `height` pixels tall: 0 at the focus, never over `most`. The CPU twin of the shader's.

signatures.code: blurRadius(depth: number, look: OpticsLook, fov: number, height: number): number

entries.name: sharpRange
entries.doc: The nearest and farthest distances drawn no blurrier than `sharp` pixels: the slice in focus. `far` is Infinity when everything behind the focus is that sharp.

signatures.code: sharpRange(look: OpticsLook, fov: number, height: number, sharp?: number): { near: number; far: number }

entries.name: glowShare
entries.doc: How much of a pixel's light glows: nothing under the knee, then rising smoothly to all of it a third of the knee higher. The CPU twin of the shader's.

entries.name: rolledOff
entries.doc:
A brightness after the film's shoulder: unchanged up to `start`, then closing on 1 ever more slowly and never
passing it. The lens scales a pixel's whole color by this over its brightest channel, so its hue holds. The CPU
twin of the shader's.

modules.title: Colliders
modules.doc:
Colliders: simple solid shapes laid over a scan or a scene, which has none of its own. A scan is a cloud of blobs
with nothing to stand on or bump into; a box for the table, a cylinder for the mug and a slab for the floor give
feet a ground (`groundOf`, the `Ground` that `plantFeet` takes) and bodies something to stay out of (`pushOut`).

A shape is a box, a ball or an upright cylinder, turned only about the upright, which is what furniture and floors
need and keeps every question (how far, how high, where a ray lands) a few lines. `writeColliderGlb` saves them as
ordinary glTF nodes with a mesh each, so the file opens anywhere as shapes, and `readColliderGlb` reads them back
exactly.

entries.name: Collider
entries.doc: One solid shape.

props.name: shape
props.doc: A box, a ball, or a cylinder standing along y.

props.name: center
props.doc: Its middle, in world space.

props.name: size
props.doc: A box's half sizes; a ball's radius (the first value); a cylinder's radius and half height.

props.name: turn
props.doc: Degrees it is turned about the upright (a ball and a cylinder look the same turned).

props.name: name
props.doc: What it stands for, if named: 'floor', 'table'.

entries.name: SMALLEST
entries.doc: The smallest a shape's size may be dragged to.

entries.name: colliderDistance
entries.doc: Signed distance from p to the shape's surface: negative inside.

entries.name: topAt
entries.doc: How high the shape's top is over the point (x, z) of the floor, or undefined where it is not over it.

signatures.code: topAt(c: Collider, x: number, z: number): number | undefined

entries.name: groundOf
entries.doc:
The ground the shapes make, for `plantFeet` and anything else that asks how high the floor is at (x, z): the
highest top under the point, and `base` where there is none.

signatures.code: groundOf(colliders: readonly Collider[], base?: number): (x: number, z: number) => number

entries.name: groundBelow
entries.doc: The same ground, but only tops no more than `step` above `from`: a shape too tall to step onto is a wall, not a floor.

signatures.code: groundBelow(colliders: readonly Collider[], from: number, step: number, base?: number): (x: number, z: number) => number

entries.name: pushOut
entries.doc: A ball of `radius` at p, moved the shortest way out of every shape it is in (a few rounds, for corners).

signatures.code: pushOut(colliders: readonly Collider[], p: ArrayLike<number>, radius?: number): Vec3

entries.name: rayCollider
entries.doc: How far along a ray (a unit `direction`) it first meets the shape, or undefined if it misses within `far`.

signatures.code: rayCollider(c: Collider, origin: ArrayLike<number>, direction: ArrayLike<number>, far?: number): number | undefined

entries.name: pickCollider
entries.doc: The shape a ray meets first: its index and how far along, or undefined.

signatures.code: pickCollider(colliders: readonly Collider[], origin: ArrayLike<number>, direction: ArrayLike<number>): { index: number; t: number } | undefined

entries.name: wireOf
entries.doc:
The shape as lines to draw over a picture: each entry is a run of points to join. A box's twelve edges, a cylinder's
two rims and four sides, a ball's three great circles. `steps` is how many points a circle gets.

entries.name: Handle
entries.doc: A handle on a shape: where it is, the way it pulls, and which of the shape's sizes it changes.

props.name: key
props.doc: Which of the shape's sizes it changes.

props.name: at
props.doc: Where it is, in world space.

props.name: axis
props.doc: The way it pulls (a unit vector): out along it grows the shape.

entries.name: handlesOf
entries.doc: The handles that size a shape: one on each face that matters (a box's three, a cylinder's side and top, a ball's side).

entries.name: resized
entries.doc: The shape with one size changed by `by` (pulling its handle out or in); never smaller than `SMALLEST`.

signatures.code: resized(c: Collider, key: 0 | 1 | 2, by: number): Collider

entries.name: placed
entries.doc: The shape scaled about the origin and then shifted: for a scan that is resized and stood somewhere else.

signatures.code: placed(c: Collider, scale: number, shift?: ArrayLike<number>): Collider

entries.name: guessColliders
entries.doc:
A first guess for a scan: a slab for the floor (its top at `floor`, reaching well past the thing) and a box round
what was kept (`lo` to `hi`, from the floor up). Either is left out when it would have no size.

signatures.code: guessColliders(lo: ArrayLike<number>, hi: ArrayLike<number>, floor: number): Collider[]

entries.name: ColliderFileError
entries.doc: Thrown when a file holds no shapes we can read.

entries.name: writeColliderGlb
entries.doc:
The shapes as a .glb: a node each, placed and turned, with a mesh of its surface so the file opens anywhere, our
own exact note in the node's `extras`, and the Khronos draft extensions for physics shapes (`KHR_implicit_shapes`,
`KHR_physics_rigid_bodies`; used, not required) so an engine that knows them takes the shapes as colliders.

entries.name: isColliderGlb
entries.doc: Whether these bytes are a .glb of colliders (ours, or another tool's with the physics shape extensions).

entries.name: readColliderGlb
entries.doc:
Reads the shapes back from a .glb: ours exactly, from each node's own note; another tool's from the physics shape
extensions (boxes, spheres and upright cylinders; a turn about the upright is kept, any other is dropped). At most
`most` shapes. Throws `ColliderFileError` when the file holds none.

entries.name: SKIN_EXTENSION
entries.doc:
Rigged splats in a .glb.

The blobs are a KHR_gaussian_splatting primitive (POINTS, with SCALE,
ROTATION, OPACITY and the degree-0 color as extra attributes), so any
viewer that knows that extension shows the creature. The rig uses only
standard glTF: JOINTS_0 and WEIGHTS_0 on the same primitive, a skin, joint
nodes, and animation channels on those nodes.

What glTF doesn't say is how a skinned *splat* turns, since a blob has a
rotation and a shape as well as a position. Our extension,
BLOBSCAPE_gaussian_skinning, says so: blob centers follow the usual linear
blend, and each blob's rotation is the weighted average of its bones'
rotations. It's listed as used, not required, so viewers that don't know it
still load the file, and most will show the creature standing still. The
full rule is written up in docs/rigged-splats.md.

Morphs are standard glTF morph targets on the same primitive (POSITION
deltas, animated as the mesh node's `weights`), and our second extension,
BLOBSCAPE_gaussian_morphs, adds what a splat needs beside its center: a SHAPE
attribute per target (the morph's local 3×3 map minus identity, morph.ts) and
which targets are in-betweens of one morph. Viewers that know glTF morphs but
not the extension move the centers right and leave the shapes as they were.

entries.name: MORPH_EXTENSION
entries.doc:
The glTF extension that says how each morph target changes a splat's shape, and which targets are one morph's
in-betweens.

entries.name: SHAPE_ATTRIBUTE
entries.doc: The morph target attribute holding each splat's shape change, G = J − I, as a column-major MAT3.

entries.name: SKIN_RULE
entries.doc: How a skinned blob turns and grows: the spec is docs/rigged-splats.md.

entries.name: Clip
entries.doc: An animation: keys for each bone at shared times.

props.name: name
props.doc: The clip's name.

props.name: times
props.doc: Seconds.

props.name: rotations
props.doc: Per bone, a rotation key per time (x, y, z, w).

props.name: offsets
props.doc: Per bone that moves, an offset key per time (x, y, z) on top of its rest place; missing for bones that never move.

props.name: sizes
props.doc: Per bone that grows or shrinks, a uniform scale key per time; missing for bones that keep their size.

props.name: weights
props.doc: Each morph's weight per time (times × morphs, a key's weights together); missing for a clip that leaves them at 0.

entries.name: Rigged
entries.doc: Everything a rigged .glb holds: the blobs, their skin, the skeleton, its clips and any morphs.

props.name: name
props.doc: The model's name.

props.name: blobs
props.doc: The blobs in the rest pose.

props.name: skin
props.doc: Which bones move each blob, and by how much.

props.name: skeleton
props.doc: The bones.

props.name: clips
props.doc: Its animations.

props.name: morphs
props.doc: Blend shapes on the blobs (morph.ts), applied to the rest blobs before skinning; clips key their weights.

entries.name: recordClip
entries.doc:
Records a clip by posing the skeleton at `fps` across `seconds`. Rotations
are kept for every bone; offsets and sizes only for bones that use them.
`weights`, if given, says each morph's weight at a time, and is keyed too.
Leaves the skeleton posed at the end.

signatures.code: recordClip(name: string, sk: Skeleton, pose: (sk: Skeleton, t: number) => void, seconds: number, fps?: number, weights?: (t: number) => ArrayLike<number>): Clip

entries.name: sampleWeights
entries.doc:
Each morph's weight from a clip at time t (looping, interpolating keys), into
`out`. False, with `out` all 0, when the clip keys no weights.

signatures.code: sampleWeights(clip: Clip | undefined, t: number, out: Float32Array): boolean

entries.name: sampleClip
entries.doc: Poses the skeleton from a clip at time t (looping), interpolating keys.

signatures.code: sampleClip(clip: Clip, sk: Skeleton, t: number): void

entries.name: writeRiggedGlb
entries.doc:
Writes blobs, bones, clips and morphs as a .glb: the KHR_gaussian_splatting standard with ordinary glTF skins and
animation, plus the two Blobscape extensions. Blender and game engines open its bones and clips.

entries.name: MORPH_RULE
entries.doc: How a morph target's shape change is applied: J = I + Σ w·SHAPE, and the splat's covariance becomes J Σ Jᵀ (docs/rigged-splats.md).

entries.name: writeRiggedMeshGlb
entries.doc:
A solid, skinned triangle mesh with the same bones and clips: what Blender,
Godot, Unity and three.js open as an ordinary animated model. Colors are
per vertex (glTF wants them linear, so they're converted from the blobs'
display color); the material is marked unlit, since the blobs' colors
already have their lighting baked in. Viewers that don't know
KHR_materials_unlit light it as a plain matte surface.

signatures.code: writeRiggedMeshGlb(r: { name: string; mesh: SplatMesh; skeleton: Skeleton; clips: Clip[] }): Uint8Array

entries.name: GlbError
entries.doc: Thrown when a file can't be read as a rigged .glb; its message says why.

entries.name: readRiggedGlb
entries.doc: Reads a .glb written by `writeRiggedGlb`, or any KHR_gaussian_splatting file with a skin whose joints have no rest rotation.

modules.title: Rigged models to splats
modules.doc:
A rigged model to splats, keeping its rig: an ordinary skinned glTF (a .glb from Blender, Mixamo or
a game kit: triangles, JOINTS_0/WEIGHTS_0, a skin and its animations) read into our bones and clips, then its
surface covered in flat blobs that hang on the same bones with the weights the mesh gave its corners. Pure: the
page decodes texture images and hands them in as `Texture`s.

Our bones have no rest rotation: a bone is its head, posed by a turn about it. A glTF joint carries any rest
frame, so each frame of a clip is read as what the skin does, not what the nodes say: joint j's skin matrix is
S = G·IBM (its world matrix now times its inverse bind matrix), which takes the bind pose to the posed one. Its
linear part is our bone's world turn (times its scale) and it carries the bind head (where IBM⁻¹ puts the joint)
to where the joint is now. Local turns, offsets and sizes follow from those, so the blobs land where the mesh's
vertices would.

entries.name: SkinnedModel
entries.doc: An ordinary skinned model as `readSkinnedGlb` reads it: its triangles, their bone weights, our bones and its clips.

props.name: name
props.doc: The model's name.

props.name: mesh
props.doc: The triangles in the bind pose.

props.name: joints
props.doc: Per vertex, four of our bone indices and their weights (summing to 1).

props.name: weights
props.doc: Per vertex, the weights of those four bones.

props.name: bones
props.doc: Our bones, parents first.

props.name: clips
props.doc: Its animations, sampled onto our bones.

props.name: images
props.doc: Texture images, still encoded, which `mesh.tex` points at.

entries.name: MODEL_FPS
entries.doc: Keys a second when a clip is read: glTF keys may sit anywhere in time, ours sit evenly.

entries.name: readSkinnedGlb
entries.doc:
Reads a skinned .glb: the first mesh node with a skin, its triangles in the bind pose with colors and texture
coordinates, the skin's joints as our bones (parents first), and every animation sampled as our clips.

entries.name: SplatOptions
entries.doc: Options for `splatModel`.

props.name: count
props.doc: How many blobs to lay on the surface.

props.name: height
props.doc: The model's height once fitted, standing on y = 0 and centered over the origin; left as the file has it when missing.

props.name: textures
props.doc: Decoded texture images, in the order of `model.images`.

props.name: base
props.doc: The color of a surface with neither vertex colors nor a texture (sRGB).

props.name: seed
props.doc: The same seed scatters the blobs the same way.

entries.name: splatModel
entries.doc:
The model as rigged splats: `count` flat blobs scattered over its triangles by area (the same seed gives the same
blobs), each lying on its triangle, colored from the vertex colors or the texture at that point, and hung on the
bones the triangle's corners hang on, weighted by how near each corner is. Bones and clips come with it, fitted
to `height` when given.
